utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we start, Mr. Theunens, I'd like to remind you again that you're still bound by the solemn declaration given at the beginning of your testimony. I put on the record that although late yesterday after court you were - and I'm developing a bad habit in this respect - that you were instructed not to speak with anyone about your testimony. Mr. Bakrac, are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yesterday, before we adjourned, we discussed Arkan. I would like to take it up from where we stopped. You were discussing a document relating to the battle at Luzac. Earlier on, you told us that it was your understanding that in combat operations Arkan was under JNA command. I'm interested in page 2, so I'd like to show you a P exhibit, 1187.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call it up, please in e-court. My apologies, it seems that we've got a wrong document. P1187. Maybe I'm mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you must have seen this document because it is part of your report. It's very short. This is consent or approval where Milan Milovanovic agrees to the expenses of the Territorial Defence centre for the training of volunteers, being reimbursed to the socially owned enterprise Dalj, which will make the payment in a timely fashion and cover the costs of the centre. We don't have the exact date, but we can see that the document is from 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a reference in the left top corner, indeed, to the registration number of the document which indicates or would indicate that it's from 1992, but I don't see any strong other indication.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Theunens, we can agree that the -- there is the stamp of the Ministry of Defence, but do you know who Milan Milovanovic was at the time -- or I'm sorry, Milan Milanovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that Milan Milanovic has been minister of defence of the -- the SAO SBWS, but I'm not sure anymore whether he also held that position once the SAO SBWS joined the Republic of Serbian Krajina, I mean the self-declared Republic of Serbian Krajina, RSK, in spring 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Theunens. So Ministry of Defence -- or, rather, Defence Minister Milan Milanovic appears to state that the TO training centre in Erdut -- or, rather, that that particular training centre is one of the TO and that it seems to receive financing from private companies present in the area. Will you agree with me that this is what the document reflects?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what this document reflects, but the reality is more complicated. And if you want, I can explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Perhaps later on. What I'm interested in is that this is the document that you included in your report and that did you not have reason to doubt it. This Erdut training centre for volunteers, is it the one that was used by Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, and the Serbian Volunteer Guard?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. But I would like just to add, in relation to the financing of the training centre, there is, for example, P1078, which is discussed on page 72 of part 2 of my report, where additional information on the alleged financing of that training centre is provided. P1078 is a 1st Military District security organ's report. And then let me just explain the reference to TO. In the relevant legislation, i.e., the 1974 constitution and the 1982 Law on All People's Defence, it is stated that the armed forces consists of the JNA and the TO and that any armed structure that is not part of the JNA or the police will be considered part of the TO. And I have indicated in my report, in order to give a kind of a legal flavour to what was happening as a part of this campaign or -- campaign -- or these activities to regularise the status of volunteers, we see that quite often the name TO is used whereas in fact we're talking about volunteers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, if I read the document, it is a bit unclear that the socially-owned enterprise Dalj will pay for the expenses. It reads: "We hereby agree that the expenses of the Territorial Defence centre will be reimbursed to the socially-owned enterprise Dalj which will make the payment and the currency time-limit reimbursed to and payments to be made by ..." It may be my lack of understanding of the English language.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] no, Your Honour, I think the translation is perfectly fine. I can ask Mr. Theunens if he ever came across information and if he knows that this is the case based on the constitution that this company of Dalj is one that is present in Eastern Slavonia, and they were duty-bound by virtue of minister's decision to finance the defence effort, and I'm referring to these socially-owned and private companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will reply by reading out what is included in P1078. And I'm quoting from page 73 of part 2 of my report, where it states -- I mean, the document states that: "Arkan's training centre in Erdut is financed in various ways which have not yet fully been analysed according to security organs, adding that it is known that it is financed by the SPS, i.e., the Serbian Socialist Party, from within the country and from abroad as well as by numerous enterprises." And then the Dalj farm is included or is mentioned as one of these enterprises whereby, according to P1078, the Dalj farm is contributing to the payment of the costs of the training centre on the instructions of Mr. Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, your microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just verifying whether my understanding of -- if it would have read "will be reimbursed by," then I would expect Dalj to contribute to the cost; but here it says "will be reimbursed to." But it could be that my understanding of the English language is insufficient in this respect. But I'd rather like to understand what I read.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could I -- perhaps could I seek the assistance of native speaking persons. Mr. Jordash, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I think Your Honour would be right but for the last phrase "and cover the current costs of the centre," which clears up, I think, any ambiguity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand; to be reimbursed, if something is reimbursed to someone, that any costs he may have made will be paid back to him. Which is, for me, a bit difficult to understand where on the one-hand side it says "will be reimbursed to" and at the same time that company covering the costs.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think that reimbursed is -- is an odd word and not the right word in this context. And it sits uneasily with the last phrase. But the last phrase, to me, clears up the ambiguity created by the word reimbursed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, if the one contradicts the other a bit, then it's a matter of which one will be the prevailing one. But I do understand that you say that reimbursed sounds a bit odd in your ears as well, which at least is of some consolation to me. Mr. Weber, is -- perhaps we should have it checked as far as translation is concerned, unless the original text is as ambiguous as the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Two things, Your Honours. One, with respect to the text of the document, reimbursed could relate to past costs and then there could be present costs; so these could be two separate matters. Also, secondly, I believe there may be further evidence related to this in this document and upcoming testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll further look at it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... nevertheless, if someone would -- would verify the translation, whether it's ambiguity in the original text or whether it's an imprecise translation. I think it would be good to at least know that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can only add that I agree with my learned friend Mr. Weber and his interpretation of the matter, that it may relate to past and present costs. As far as we are concerned, the expert witness has given a satisfactory answer. Can we look at P1189 now, please. I'd only like to look at the time-line. We looked at the document from December 1991 and we saw, based on the stamp, that it was the TO training centre in Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Have a look at another document which seems to have come from the HQ of the training centre for volunteers, dated the 15th of May, 1992. And we see the heading "Territorial Defence Centre for Special Training," and it is addressed to the municipal secretariat for health and social protection, administration for veterans and invalids of war, and we see Zeljko Arkan as the signatory. So will you agree with me that also in the months of May 1992 the Erdut training centre was a centre for -- a TO centre for volunteers? The text even mentions that this is the TO training centre under the command, or running, of Arkan. There's date which relates to Ranko Strbac, but we can see that the centre was under the command of Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan; it follows from the text itself.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, to be precise, the September 1991 document we saw yesterday had indeed a heading of "Special Training Centre for the Territorial Defence of SBWS" as well as a stamp referring to a training centre for volunteers. Here at the end we see -- I mean, the paragraph that starts with "thus we acknowledge," it states that the person stayed with the Serbian Volunteer Guard, Territorial Defence centre for special training of SBWS, under command of Raznjatovic. Again I repeat what I said earlier, that is, that the name "TO" is only used to give what I would call a legal cover to these kind of structures, as the legislation foresaw that any armed structure that is not part of the JNA or the police is part of the TO. I use this document in my report on page 75 of part 2 to indicate that at least one member of the MUP Serbia, I mean the person indicated in the document, was -- or underwent training, as well as he participated in combat activities in SBWS, according to this document. And he underwent --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I have two questions for you now. First, where did you obtain information to the effect that Ranko Strbac was a member of the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My conclusion is based on the fact that he has a personal identification number according -- with the MUP Belgrade according to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Then both I and my colleague Petrovic and Bosa Vulic, our colleague, are all members of the MUP. I don't hold it against you; perhaps you didn't go investigating the matter as far, or the translation was wrong, but the identity paper number O88046 was issued by the MUP of Belgrade. My identity card also mentions - and I can photocopy mine and present it here - as well as the identity card of all my colleagues, was issued by the MUP of Belgrade. So MUP features here as the authority issuing the identity paper and does not testify to his membership of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the simple question would have been: Looking at the number of the identification, have you considered the possibility that it was just issued by the MUP in Belgrade, instead of indicating that someone was among the MUP Belgrade people? That's a very simple question, takes approximately one-fourth of the time you take, and we have an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did not verify whether -- or I was not in a position to verify whether this registration number was just a common registration number for anyone who would obtain an ID number or an ID card in -- from what appears to be MUP Belgrade, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you have not considered that possibility --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and your conclusion was based on an unverified assumption.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. And, of course, I would be -- I would be willing to review it, if proven incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you say, If it can be shown or let's see if it's the case. Do you have any doubt in that regard or do you think we should investigate the matter and substantiate this? Or perhaps we should give you time until after the break for you to state your opinion on this.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the opinion is clear. The opinion is that Mr. Theunens has not verified the matter you just raised. Now, it's up to you whether to invite Mr. Theunens or to do anything. At this moment, what he said is on loose grounds. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I would like to clarify another matter. If my understanding is correct - if I'm mistaken, I apologise - in relation to the document we looked at yesterday and the one we are looking at now, you seemed to have referred to a difference in the heading or the stamps; am I right, or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, what I was saying, that the document you showed yesterday, which is a December 1991 document, had a heading "Special Training Centre of the TO of SBWS" as well as a stamp or another heading a bit lower on the first page referring to a volunteer training centre. And just to be complete, when the TO of the RSK is renamed or transformed into the PJM, the Special Police or milicija units, the training centre becomes an RSK MUP training centre, and this happens after May or after November 1992, but the training centre and -- remains the same. It is just the name that changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now look at a video-clip which has to do with what we discussed earlier where Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, himself, speaks about the command or the body under whose command he is. It's 2D324. And can we start from 01:42:28 to 01:42:52. So it's half a minute. I can see my learned friend on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution wants to put on the record that this is one of the documents that it received notice of at -- on the 31st of October, 2010, at 5.44 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have the video-clip played.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Your boys are executing all the tasks. All I can say is the fact that they came by themselves contributes a lot to that, that -- the fact that they are volunteers. And I want to re-emphasise, you know, yourself, that we are under the command of the Territorial Defence of the Serbian Autonomous Region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem and that the Territorial Defence itself is under the command of the armed forces of the Yugoslav People's Army."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In support of all the physical evidence, what just Arkan stated about the structure under whose command they are or whom they belong to, would you have anything to say which would challenge what we've just heard in the footage?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I would be able to challenge the footage, I would have to know when it was filmed and where it was filmed and about which specific situation Mr. Raznjatovic was talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I will try to give you the appropriate references, but in the meantime could we please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at P1070.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just with respect to 2D234 that was just shown, the Prosecution's a little bit confused. Is counsel not going further with this, or are they going to be going further in terms of tendering this exhibit. Because based on the answer it's unclear if they are intending to go further with what's been presented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Bakrac doesn't give it any follow-up, then it's irrelevant in the context of the testimony of this witness, I would say. Unless any other link is established. Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I shall try to find the time and the date when this was actually stated. I think that we have the wrong document on the screen. I may have misspoken. It is P1079 that I'm asking for. The 65 ter number is 1454.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I think that you already know this document. You are looking at it now too.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed I have mentioned that document. For example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- before we continue, the document is under seal. I do not know whether this has any effect for the testimony. Mr. Weber, I'm also looking at you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I apologise for not catching it. If we could just not have the document broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- that was already -- Madam Registrar was cautious enough to ... but I do not know whether this has any effect on the -- on the testimony to be broadcasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I don't believe so. If there's reference to identity of a source in the document, we'd ask that counsel refrain and the witness refrain from expressing the identity of the source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So would you please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That was not my intention anyway. As far as I understand things, this is information provided by the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if I understand this document correctly, it has to do with the mistreatment of volunteers of the JNA. However, if I understand things correctly, and my question to you is whether you understand it properly, namely the volunteers from Ruma, a few of them, were transferred to Erdut as organised by Major Vuckovic from the Ruma garrison, and they ended up at Arkan's training centre in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we could scroll down in the English document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that what I am stating, which is the essence of this document, is on the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, could you -- I don't remember what the question is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. My question is whether you agree that from this document one can see that from Ruma, which is in the territory of Serbia, there are volunteers coming, as organised by Major Vuckovic from the Ruma garrison, and they're ending up at Arkan's training centre for the TO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With the additional comment that it appears to be rather in a disorganised manner that they end up in Arkan's training centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, but what is relevant for me is that they leave Serbia as volunteers in the organisation of Major Vuckovic from the Ruma garrison; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what this document states, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it also correct - and that is important for me because we have also been dealing with rumours here, in part - is it correct that these persons who had claimed that they had been mistreated at Arkan's centre also claimed that they had seen Arkan kill Ante Kedjo, a volunteer, and that then when the security organs checked this it was established that Ante Kedjo was alive and being treated at the Mitrovica hospital? Can that also not be seen from this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, if a document says there was a report that someone was killed, but that person was treated in hospital, what -- I mean, this Chamber can read, isn't it? If you want to draw our attention to certain matters, fine. But unless you expect any specific information, to receive such information from Mr. Theunens, but that's what the document says, isn't it? You could also ask, Is it true that the document is of this date, is it true that the document ... that's all clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why spend time on asking questions which could be answered by any person, unless there's any reason to believe that what is in the document, for example, the date is incorrect, if you expect that the witness would have any special knowledge about it? But otherwise, it's just going through documents asking someone to read and then to say, Is this what it says. Of course it says what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understand. You are the quite right. I do apologise to you. The first question was a long one. But since we've been dealing with the document anyway and since Mr. Theunens in his report relied on some unverified information, I just wanted to illustrate for the Trial Chamber that sometimes it happens that somebody says, like here two people said that Arkan killed such and such a person, and ultimately this person proved to be alive and treated in hospital. So I just wanted to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to cases like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The proper way of doing that is the following: The first you would have asked Mr. Theunens, You agree with me that this document demonstrates that sometimes rumours, upon verification, appeared not to be true; that's one. Second, Do you have any specific knowledge on this rumour. Third, Are you aware of any similar rumours which might not reflect reality. That's -- that's apparently what you want to establish. So please then focus your questions on those matters. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you very much indeed. Yes, that would have been a better course, and I put all of this together into a complicated question that was unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let me not repeat all of that. Can you respond to that question - if not, we are going to move on - that His Honour, the Presiding Judge, had just phrased and basically helped me in doing so?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. I mean, there's a lot of information in this report about different issues and the data on the alleged killing whereby the two volunteers do not claim that they saw, as you stated, they didn't see Arkan kill the person, but they simply stated that he had killed -- allegedly killed that volunteer. That that information, after verification, was incorrect. Now, one would also verify the other information if one was to rely on the information included in the report as part of the methodology I explained in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any specific information about this incident which, upon verification, seemed to be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question: Did you often find in the documentation you reviewed or in any other source that rumours existed which turned out to be not in accordance with reality? If you say it seldom happened, we have an indication. If you say, Well, that's what I found several times, then we would have an indication as well, or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Obviously there are a lot of rumours circulating on, for example, alleged crimes. Now, I only discussed crimes when I had what I considered reliable documents. And I always tried to look for corroboration for these documents. So I only included such documents in my report. And I -- for example, I refrained from using open-source documents, in particular, open source documents prepared by what I would call the opposing side. Now, information is information. It's part of the intelligence process or intelligence cycle. And, of course, it needs to be verified. And sometimes it's explicitly mentioned. I mean, at one time it was explicitly mentioned in one of the information reports that there was -- that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let me stop you. The simple question was whether it -- what approximately the frequency was in finding information in documents which by other sources were falsified, such as here. Here it's even in the same document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honours. No, I -- as I tried to explain, I find -- I found or identified a pattern in the different documents I reviewed, and this pattern in relation to the activities of the different volunteer groups are reflected in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we are going to analyse that. But for the time being, we haven't got time to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please view video-clip 2D166.1. For the record, Your Honours, this is -- this starts from 07:38 and goes up until 09:21. So this is from the Belgrade TV news. The footage is from Slavonia in 1991, the 25th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution want to put on the record that we received notice of this on the 31st of October, 2010, at 5.44 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I want the record to reflect, in terms of this document and the previous one, that this is video material that we received from the OTP. Could that please be reflected in the record. We did perhaps provide notification a bit late, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's on the record as well. Please proceed. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just -- I don't mean to ensue a debate, but even though that it comes from the Office of the Prosecutor, there's a large volume of material --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course that's -- that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- and we would appreciate notification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. Weber, that's exactly the reason why I limited myself to saying that's on the record as well. Of course the fact that it is part of your collection in itself does not answer the question. No one expects you to have full, accurate, and actual knowledge of all the documents that were disclosed to the Defence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let us please view this video-clip.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "How did the representatives of the Croatian armed forces, whose crimes you have just seen, present themselves on the eve of their surrender to the representatives of the JNA? "They were already sacrificed and deceived by their leadership which abandoned them in the lairs of Borovo Naselje and Vukovar and order them to stay there and die. With no way out, they are emerging from their mousetraps in search of salvation. And all this from the same army, the JNA, which, until the day, before they slammed as being a Chetnik-Bolshevik occupier and for which they lay and wait perfidiously with snipers. Several commanders, low-ranking as they now claim, were received by the commander of the Novi Sad Corps, Major-General Andrija Biorcevic. "We are doing our job, and you're doing yours. I feel for the victims. If you are guilty, you will answer for it. If you are not guilty, this is known. "And now, as if somebody else, not them, had slaughtered Darko Mirkovic and Mirkovic and Cvijeta Perlic from Borovo Naselje only because they were Serbs. As if somebody else, not them, used a Bunsen burner to burn the seriously wounded Djordje Vukicevic from the village of Luzac. It is only now that they would talk as men, as human beings, with the JNA general to explain, to promise, that they will convince the other criminals not to die in vain, to save their skin as well. If only, as they had humbly promised, they were also to put in an effort to end the killing of people, you're people and our people."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I keep forgetting, Your Honour, to pause. I do apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we discussed this, and during the direct and re-direct you said that the Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, was under the JNA and combat operations. We see here our discussion with prisoners that is conducted by Andrija Biorcevic, commander of the Novi Sad Corps. Could you identify who it was sitting next to him during this conversation with the prisoners? Actually, let's deal with that first so that we can then move on. On his left, did you see Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, does this go beyond your conclusions that it was only in combat operations that Arkan was under the command of the JNA? This is a conversation or an interview or an interrogation of Croatian ZNGs, and Arkan is sitting right next to General Biorcevic, commander of the Novi Sad Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it doesn't indicate anything. I mean, the seating arrangements, here, for example, for this video, there's no possibility to draw any conclusions as to what the command and control relations were. Anyway, if we want to discussion the relations - and I even say the personal relations - between General Biorcevic and Zeljko Raznjatovic, I would like to refer to P1219, which is discussed on page 94 of part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I have only one more question in this regard. So this is not a combat operation, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, you are now telling whether it's a combat operation or not. Mr. Theunens, when you testified about Arkan working in the JNA command structures during combat operations, would you limit that to the battle-field only, or would that include all the activities directly related to such combat operations even after the direct combat activities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, my conclusion is limited to the activities that are a strict part of the combat operations, i.e., the briefing prior to the launching of the combat operation, from then until the end of the combat operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would that include such type of activity - which, by the way, I do not know whether this is why this was broadcasted, why it was recorded at all - but would that include also a kind of - how do you say that? - a kind of a briefing after the end of the operations, or once the battle was fought they would go separate ways and not even have a conversation with each other anymore?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They could still have a conversation afterwards, but I haven't seen any -- any documents that indicate that Arkan was subordinated to the JNA after the conclusion of specific combat operations. I mean, just to end the answer, documentary evidence for the activities of OG North - at least there is -- the documentary evidence available to the OTP - is very scarce. We discussed the Luzac attack yesterday, and I have the quote by General Biorcevic, and that's it. Sorry, and the documents of military security organs where they state that Arkan acts independently. So that's the basis for my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have P500 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: At one point yesterday you said that Arkan's centre in Erdut changed, that it was the Territorial Defence at first and that it changed later on. I would like us to have a look at this document. And could you please explain to me, as a military expert, how you would interpret this. Actually, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It's brief. Please have a look at it in detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This document also is under seal and not to be shown to the public. Any reference to individuals, therefore, should not be specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the document is brief. Could I please ask you to focus on the document, and I'm going to put a question to you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is what I'm putting to you. This is how I read the document, and you are going to tell me whether I'm right or not. When the Serb Army of the Serb Republic of the Krajina -- and it says here, in relation to this one person, that he was a soldier from the 21st of January to the 23rd of December, 1999, it says that the camp in Erdut is growing into a military post and becoming part of the Army of the Serb Republic of the Krajina. Do you agree with that? We have here this military post. The commander is Colonel Milorad Ulemek, Erdut. Do you agree with my observation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not entirely. We know, for example, from P1244, that in November 1992, the RSK political and military authorities implement a decision to transform the Special Police, I mean, the PJM, which was actually a re-badging of the Territorial Defence. They transformed this Special Police into the SVK, so the Serbian Army of the Krajina. And we see that even if the structure of these units remains unchanged, the name is changed. And in my view, this also applies to the training centre. Since it's now given a military name, it should also have a military post number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if I understood you correctly, this was the sequence of events: The centre at Erdut commanded by Arkan at first, that is to say at the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992, was a Territorial Defence centre; then when the government was established and when the plan was implemented, the peace plan, then it became -- I mean, that centre became a Special Police centre, or rather, after that, all of that was brought together -- or, rather, it grew into the Army of the Republic of the Serb Krajina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe to be more precise, there were a number of changes in the name, not only of the training centre but also of military units in the RSK because, as you know, the Vance Plan foresaw a demilitarisation and disarming of all military structures, but the Serbs in the Krajina were allowed to keep a police force. So in order to circumvent that, the TO, which was still existing until early 1992, was renamed or re-batched into Special Police. But then in the course of 1992 - and I think the first decision was taken in May, which was implemented in November 1992 - the PJM, units which were in fact re-batched TO units, were re-batched again into military units. And that also applied to the training centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We are discussing units of the Serbian Autonomous District of SBWS, is that right, when we are talking about the changes that were taking place?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this happened all over the RSK. I mean, the RSK was declared end of 1991. And I believe that in February or March or April 1992 the SAO SBWS joined the RSK. So at this moment in time, we're talking about the RSK. And this can be also found on pages 109 and 110 of part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Theunens. I have a very simple question: Did you come across a single document -- we were looking at documents from 1994, and I'm going to show you a document -- documents from 1995. Did you find a single document dating back to the period between 1991 and 1995 to the effect that the MUP of the Republic of Serbia had anything to do with this camp or any sort of control over it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, there are, in my report, a number of information reports from security organs from, I think, even from 1996, but I would have to look into them, security organs of the VJ, making mention of the camp in Erdut, but would I have to look in my report to find the exact reference. There's just one point I would like to add to the document we see now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first receive a full answer to the question. Did you find any -- I mean, what you said is that security organs of the VJ were making -- were mentioned in the report, which, in itself, doesn't establish anything to the MUP of Serbia, because that was what the question was about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you come across any document in which a link, involvement, as Mr. Bakrac said, anything to do with between MUP and the Erdut camp? MUP Serbia and the Erdut camp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, at this stage I don't recall, but I will look during the break. And if I can identify a document in my report, I will -- I would like to come back to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I know some of these questions are kind of like pop quiz questions as to how many documents. The Prosecution has looked at this and is able to provide lists. This would also be for the Chamber's guidance, as to the documents that refer to it in the report. This would also shorten possible re-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would prepare such a list and if you would provide a that to Mr. Bakrac, then we could see whether the Chamber could use that as well and whether it would be a useful interim instrument to focus questions to the -- to Mr. Theunens. Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I want to make this quite clear. Outside of these organs of security of the Army of Yugoslavia, I'd like to know whether there were any others.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at another document, 2D308. In the B/C/S it's page 1, and page 2 in English, item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'll take you through it to make this quick. It is the Operational Group 10. It's the 13th of October, 1995, combat order. Under 2 it is stated: "The units of OG-10, including the following:" And now says, among others: "Serbian Volunteer Guard squad, MUP, and 1/27 mtbr of the present combat disposition," et cetera. It's a rather longish document, so I've only directed you to what I'm interested in. If you want to, you can look through the document to see the context. And it was signed by Lieutenant-General Momir Talic. You can look at the document if need be, and my question is: Did, in 1995, the then-commander Momir Talic, the then-commander of the 1st Krajina Corps, issue an order to the Serbian Volunteer Guard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection to the question. Just if Mr. Bakrac plans on tendering this document, if we could please be informed of the origin of the document and where it originates from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, any ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is a document from an OTP collection. I can see that it bears an ERN number. And that's where my assistants found it. I can give you the ERN number. The first page is 0130-8230 and the last page is 0130-8233.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. We can further look it up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let me just see. I do not see the ERN number, Mr. Bakrac, but I take it that that will be verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is possible that when the document was scanned it was no longer visible. I have a B/C/S version where it's fully visible. I can give a hard copy for Their Honours and the Prosecution, or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would allow us to just briefly check that. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you agree with me that on the 13th of October, 1995, Commander Momir Talic used the Serbian Volunteer Guard in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what the document states. And I would just like to add that it is dated two weeks after P289, which was the letter from General Mladic to, among others, Radovan Karadzic in order to clarify the situation of Zeljko Raznjatovic and his volunteers in the wider Western Bosnia area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not mind, Mr. Bakrac, but what you provided to me at this moment with the ERN number on it seems to be a document which is, as far as the typewritten part is concerned, approximately the same but is not the same document because it contains -- the document on the screen contains handwritten text which doesn't appear on the one you just gave us. So the uploaded document is not the same, although it seems that the typewritten part is -- seems to be the same, but it's not the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. You are quite right. It is puzzling because the poorer copy was sent to a detachment of the Serbian Volunteer Guard, but I don't think that in essence this changes anything. I am happy with the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There two same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I say I don't see an ERN number on it and without apparently verifying, you say, Well, perhaps it's a matter of scanning. It's not a matter of scanning; it's just a different document. So would you please, before you answer such questions, first verify the accuracy of the answer you're giving. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, please look at 2D316.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just for the record, Prosecution received notice of this document on 29 October 2010 at 1.15 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we can see that the date is the 20th of September, 1995, MUP of the RS Bijeljina, Deputy Minister Tomislav Kovac. It seems to be a dispatch. Did you know that in September 1995 Mr. Tomislav Kovac was deputy minister of the interior of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the document states, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does this dispatch refer to a decision issued by the president of Republika Srpska on the 19th of September, 1995, whereby all the armed forces are to be joined in the area of responsibility of the 1st and 2nd Corps, Krajina Corps? And if you look at the item 1 referring to Doboj, is it right that, pursuant to the president's decision, Deputy Minister Tomislav Kovac issues this decision setting up a joint staff which includes Zeljko Raznjatovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zeljko Raznjatovic is mentioned on the heading, 2, "Prijedor." But otherwise the document here states what you mention, what you indicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that Mr. President is still looking at the document, may I move on to another document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we now look at 2D307.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, look at the document. It's quite short. It says: "Pursuant to Article 80 of the constitution of Republika Srpska, Article 7 of the Law on Defence, and my order, Strictly Confidential 01-1775/95, dated 30 September ..." It would appear that the president of the republic, Dr. Radovan Karadzic, authorises this -- a special unit of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska, namely the Tigers, to arrest all deserters and fugitives from the armed forces of Republika Srpska, carry out the necessary preparations with them, and hand them over to the commands of the army in order for them to be sent into combat, in addition to other forces of the military police and the police of the Ministry of the Interior. In your research, did you ever come across any statements or evidence to the effect that Ranko -- that Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, ever chased after and captured any deserters and fugitives in order to take them back to the battle-field in Republika Srpska, and I'm merely interested in hearing from you whether you ever came across any such evidence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember two distinct cases where Arkan was used to conduct such activities. There is first -- there's information - but I have not discussed it in my report - that after the Croatian incursion in the pink zone in the wider area of Maslenica, Sector South, after 22nd of January, 1993, Arkan and a number of his volunteers were sent from Erdut to the real lines of the SVK in the area in order to prevent SVK soldiers from withdrawing, i.e., to force them to fight, because obviously the soldiers were quite impressed or even scared of Arkan's reputation. A second example - and there is a document on my report in that - is that there is information that people who left the RSK after the 4th of August, 1995, including military personnel, and who tried to flee to Serbia, were stopped at the border crossings in Serbia, and able men were rounded up and brought to the -- to Arkan's training centre in Erdut where they were held, maybe also trained, but where there were also, according to the information I reviewed, cases of abuse. And this latter activity would have taken place in cooperation with the MUP Serbia. And, again, I will look during the break for the specific document reference, because I have addressed that in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at the clock, Your Honour, we seem to -- we have a difference schedule today, so would this be the right time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it would. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, over the course of the break, with respect to this document, 2D307, and any of the upcoming documents that that Mr. Bakrac would like to use, if there's any question as to what -- the origin of the document, this document we would like to know where it originated from. But if he could please inform us, that would be helpful throughout the course of the remainder of the proceedings this morning and today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, already for this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I received the document from my investigator. I will verify the source from which my investigator obtained the document over the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll hear from you. And we'll have a break, and we'll resume at quarter to 11.00. But, yes, the first thing I'd like to do after the break is to briefly, in the absence of the witness, discuss with you how the rest of the day and tomorrow morning will look like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'd like to inquire with the parties. Today we have one more morning session, three afternoon sessions. Tomorrow morning we have also two sessions. Mr. Bakrac, could you tell us already how much time you would need so as to leave ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would need far more time than I know I realistically have. I will have to focus. But at any rate, I know that I will need the morning session tomorrow. I know that I need to leave time for Mr. Weber and his examination and the admission of documents. We would need, based on the documents we have, two or three more days, but of course realistically I know that what I need is the first session tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, how much time would you need? Would the one session do?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: As of right now, the Prosecution would estimate 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which might give you some additional time, even, because we'll have to conclude tomorrow morning. The videolink is scheduled for the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, and I prefaced it with "as of right now," so I don't know what remaining matters may arise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes. Having discussed this, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Bakrac, you often apologised when I made some observations or remarks. I'm not seeking any apologies; I'm seeking focused questions. And I tried to assist you now and then, and it really saves a lot of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm grateful for your assistance. I apologise, but I have to say yet again that you know the difficult situation Mr. Petrovic and I are in and how we got into this case and that we had to deal with a great number of documents over the past years -- year, and you see the difficulty the OTP has in identifying all the various documents in the vast database they have, and I really tried to focus and go through the documents as expeditiously as I can. I urge Their Honours to bare this in mind and see this as the underlying reason for the difficulties I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may continue, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can we continue discussing the same topic as before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have P1080 on our screens. Mr. President, I apologise, I am still supposed to tell you how I obtained the document, as promised before the break. My investigator told me that he received a photocopy of the document from a potential witness of ours who was a member of the Serbian Volunteer Guard. At this time, he does not wish his name to be mentioned, so I'd like the document to be MFI'd until he will possibly appear as a witness here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no objection to that approach and leaving it MFI'd. And with respect to the current document that's being brought up, P1080, we see that that's a document to be under seal. If it could not be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I expect the parties - let's not spend too much time on it - to prepare a list of documents, then, that are used for the witness so that we can deal with them at -- in an expeditious way. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we already have the relevant document on our screen. I think that you included the document in your report. This would appear to be a report of a collaborator called Trgovac on the situation in RSK territory. It's a state security report, is it not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. We would have to look at the heading and the end of the document. If we could just go -- scroll to the end, maybe there's a signature or a stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, Mr. Theunens, there are initials at the end of the document. Let's do it this way: Under item 78, or under paragraph 78, you deal with this topic. This is section 3, paragraph 299; and in section 2 -- chapter 2, section 2, paragraphs 232, 235; and in part 2, section 4, paragraph 414; and in part 3, section 3, paragraphs 200, 265 and 267. So obviously you referred to this document repeatedly throughout your report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've used this report. Just to clarify, the paragraph numbers obviously refer to the B/C/S translation, because I don't use this numbering in my English original.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. In -- at any rate, there were some seven or eight paragraphs -- no, I'm sorry, my mistake. I was referring to footnotes. So you referred to this document seven or eight times. Is it your evidence now that you reviewed this document but you don't know whose document it is, you don't have a position on it as to what the purpose of the document was?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in my report, I identified it as a VJ intelligence report, and that conclusion must have been based on the summary I could find in the databases which provide, among other things, the origin of the document. But if it is established that it is a document from the state security, obviously I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document was included in the Prosecution's first bar table motion received pursuant to RFA 219 which are documents which include intelligence reports prepared by the counter-intelligence services of the JNA VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can confirm the same, since I've verified it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I first wanted us to establish that you referred to the document which originated from intelligence organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And let's go back to page 1 in the B/C/S, please. It's the end of page 1 in English. It's the sixth paragraph from the top. Can we have page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The paragraph reads: "The next unit is SDG, Serbian Volunteer Guard, led by Arkan. There are around 250 of them. They are accommodated in the recreation centre right next to the bridge, and there are almost 4.000 people from Krajina there. His men are all in the camp, and the men from Krajina are all on the front lines. Arkan is with the army and Perisic and is obeying only Colonel Jovanovic. He came into conflict with General Bora Ivanovic and they are not on speaking terms." Therefore, a VJ security organ states, as it would appear here, that Arkan is with the army and Perisic and listens or complies only with what Colonel Jovanovic says. Who is Colonel Jovanovic, aka "zmija" or snake, if you know, based on the research conducted?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a Colonel Jovanovic who was, at one moment in time, I think before General Loncar, in the command of the SBWS 11th Corps, i.e., the SVK unit in Eastern Slavonia, but I cannot confirm whether this is the same Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just if counsel could specifically refer to which Jovanovic he is referring to, because I see in the document there's two Jovanovic, a Miodrag and also a Zvezdan. The Miodrag appears on the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if that resolves the matter, because -- [overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Miodrag Jovanovic, aka zmija, snake.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, it doesn't clarify or it doesn't bring back my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Let's not dwell on this, and move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English -- that's page 3 in English and 2 in B/C/S. The paragraph starts as follows. Can we look at the bottom of the page. Can we scroll the English down. No, it's the next page in English, page 4, the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is what this particular intelligence source states: "I've already said that Arkan was with the army, that he knew that his Legija was a man of the DB of Serbia, but Arkan says, 'Goran, I'm not a naive man, I know I will get killed, but first I want to kill 15.000 Croats, and that's why I'm here. If the Republic of the Serbian Krajina falls into the hands of the Croats, I can't go back to Serbia, they will kill me there.'" And then he reiterates he very much obeys Colonel Jovanovic. Mr. Theunens, this document dates from September 1995. I put it to you that sometime in 1995 Legija was recruited by the state security service and in 1996 he became a part of the unit for special operations too. So I put it to you that Arkan is informed herein of the fact that a man of his was recruited by the DB and that therefore he says, Goran, I'm not a naive person; I know that I will get killed. My understanding of this is that Arkan professes not to be a stupid person and that he was aware of the fact that a man, his -- one of his men, had been recruited by the DB. So my understanding of what he says would be that he had nothing to do, whatsoever, with the DB because, number one, he would not be informed of it, and number two, he would say, Well, yes, I belonged to the DB as well. Would you read into this paragraph the same way I am doing?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily because as I mentioned during the previous days the activities and operations we have been discussing were -- I mean, it was -- attempts were undertaken to keep the allegiance of the different groups that were involved and, more specifically, to keep the involvement or the role of the authorities of the Republic of Serbia in all this secret, so there's no need for Arkan to publicise any links he had with the DB, because it would be -- actually it could be used against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: However, the Army of Yugoslavia, a security organ of the Army of Yugoslavia, says here -- they say, themselves, that Arkan is with the army and that he only listens to Colonel Jovanovic. And then this very same organ says to Arkan, warns him, that one of his men was recruited by the DB. Why would he be hiding that from the security organ, that he was a member of the DB or that he had links to the DB?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, it's the same question as the last one. It has been answered. If you want to add anything to your question [sic], feel free to do so, Mr. Theunens. If not, could you please put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was just looking in my report, Your Honours, because there are much earlier documents linking a Legija, I mean, with real name Milorad Ulemek, to the Ministry of Interior of Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now Mr. Bakrac is not asking for a chronology of that but just why Arkan would have not told that, and you have answered that question. If you want to add anything to that, please do so. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, and we skipped the first page of this document, but just so it's on the record, there is reference to Legija on the first page, at the bottom of the translation. Very bottom half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have a look at 2D276.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So, when you were discussing the attack on Zvornik, if I remember correctly, you said that in the attack in Zvornik it was only the Serb Volunteer Guard that actively participated in it. Zeljko Raznjatovic Arkan's guard and that the Army of Yugoslavia played a passive role. Please have a look at this document and tell me, since it's a Prosecution document as well, whether you had an opportunity of seeing it before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you accurately quote me because, as you would see in my report, there were also elements of the TO Loznica, and Loznica is located in the Republic of Serbia, as well as individuals belonging to a group known as the Yellow Wasps who participated in the take-over of Zvornik. And my conclusion in relation to the JNA was based on the documents of the 17th Corps I reviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So here is the document, document of the 17th Corps, since you said that they were passive, you see here a document of the 17th Corps right in front of you, so please read it and see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution's question's also directly focused on activities between the 6th and the 10th of April. I see this document is dated the 10th, discussing activities that follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record, although it might not be the appropriate way of introducing it, Mr. Weber; re-examination is. Rather than intervening in the cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, the conclusion on the -- what I call the passive role of the JNA during the take-over is based on the documents of the 17th Corps I reviewed, and they refer to the 7th, the 8th, and the 9th of -- of April. I mean, if you look in my report, page 61, part 3, there is a reference --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... there is a reference to P1392, which obviously talks about involvement of the JNA, including Arkan there, in fighting on the 11th. But that's, for me, after the actual take-over.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you are talking about the 6th of April; I am talking about a document dated a few days before that. Quite simply, we do not have documents of the 17th Corps that would corroborate either participation or non-participation before the 10th. Non-participation or participation in combat operations in Zvornik, I mean. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed these documents. We have P1388, for example, where the 17th Corps command discusses the situation in Zvornik on the 9th of April. They also talk about their activities. But there is no information in that situational report on any participation of the 17th Corps of its subordinate units in the take-over, as it took place on the 8th, 9th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one clarifying question. When you earlier said about involvement of the JNA prior or after, did you include air force? Because this seems to be specific to the extent that air-strikes are requested for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. I don't dispute the document. But the take-over took place -- I mean, it started on the 8th, and on the 9th it was finalised. And there was, of course, an aftermath. And the whole discussion about the reports of the 17th Corps consists of or is -- yeah, consists of the fact that in the reports covering the 8th and the 9th of April, the 17th Corps does not mention, based on my review, any active involvement during those days in combat operations in Zvornik. But again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not a direct answer to my question, whether you had considered the air force as well, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. I had -- I considered the documents I had in front of me for the -- I mean, for those days, 8 and 9 and before. I don't remember that there was a specific air force document, but, again, the conclusions were based on these documents. And obviously I have seen this document before, I believe, but I don't think I referred it -- I've referred to it in my report. But P1392 also talks about combat operations in the wider Zvornik area, involving the JNA and Arkan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you say that there is no information. If there is no information, does that necessarily mean that the 17th Corps did not take active participation on the 7th, 8th, and 9th in the liberation of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I think Mr. Theunens explained to us in his previous answer what his position is, that in the reporting of the 17th Corps, that nothing is said about participation and the take-over of any combat activity in relation to Zvornik. Of course, if you do not mention, there are several options: Either there's no reporting, then the absence of any information is of limited weight; either there is reporting, but that doesn't mention it. Then you have two options: Either it did not take place; or it has not been mentioned, although it did take place. I mean, this is all logic. So whether this means this yes or no, please ask Mr. Theunens whether he has any specific reasons to believe that despite that there was reporting, that no mention was made, whether there's any other indication he may have that they were not or whether they were involved. Because that's the -- these are the questions which seem to be relevant in this context. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let's do it this way. According to military doctrine, you're a military expert and you have been working as one. Arkan's Volunteer Guard, can though do anything in the zone of responsibility of the 17th Corps without the approval and knowledge of the 17th Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a question we have addressed earlier. It all depends of the situation in the area of Zvornik. Are there combat operations ongoing; yes or no? But I understand from the documents I have reviewed is that there are still, for example, functioning civilian authorities prior to the take-over. In the wider area there is civilian police. Indeed the 17th Corps is conducting a number of activities, but they cannot be -- they are not, in my view, combat activities. The reports you showed yesterday, there was no mentioning made of a front line in the area of Zvornik. So in the absence of specific documents indicating that Arkan is subordinated to the JNA, one cannot conclude what his relation with the 17th Corps at that stage is. And just to finish, P1392 mentions Arkan's or members of Arkan's Group as forces of the 1st Military District under the section of losses. Now, that is on the 11th of April, and that would indicate that then Arkan's people are considered forces of the 1st Military District. But -- and just to finish, the 17th Corps is part of the 2nd Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So if people from the 1st Military District operate in the area of the 17th Corps, that is, from a different military district, can they do that, in your view, without the approval and knowledge of the 17th Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation is different. If you look at P1392 - all that's discussed on page 61 of part 3 of my report - the members of Arkan's Group are in the area of Mali Zvornik which is on the Serbian side of the border, i.e., in the zone of responsibility of the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And when they cross the Drina, then they're in the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Military District or, rather, the 17th Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but in a [indiscernible] military district -- military doctrine, I'm sorry, this should happen, such a movement should happen in accordance with orders that have been given. I haven't seen such orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. Now I'm going to help you. I think that you did see something, and that is -- let me just find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to check. I'm not sure, but I'd rather err on the side of caution. I would like to present a 92 bis statement, so I'm not sure whether it's a protected witness. In order to be cautious, I would like to ask for private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have page -- the end of page 2 and the beginning of page 3 in B/C/S. Actually in English, I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you see this paragraph that starts with --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, what I need here is the next page, the third page. My mistake. Page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: For the sake of time, I'm just going to read this out to you, this paragraph: "In the morning hours, people started gathering in front of the police station, asking to kill these four men. I decided to move the four men to different rooms within the police station, and I also provided them with guards to protect them. In the morning, around 6.00, about 20 people were standing outside the police station, and later on the number increased. About 10.00 in the morning, I got a telephone call from a man who introduced himself as Captain Marko. He requested me to take these four men out from town and to hand them over to the army. I told him that it was very risky because of all the shooting in Zvornik. "The attack on Zvornik started around 9.30 the same morning, on the 8th of April, 1992. About 1300 hours, Colonel Boskovic from the headquarters in Belgrade called me. He requested us to release two of the four men since they were military policemen. I know that those two who were not twins were the military policemen. I asked Boskovic about the twins; he did not know who they were, and he was not interested in them either. Boskovic phoned me one more time during the day, and I informed him that everything was okay with the four men. I cannot recall at what time Boskovic phoned me the second time. "I also received a phone call from General be Jankovic from Tuzla. He also asked about the possibility to take the four men out of town. I answered him that it was very risky, and I suggested to him, as I had suggested to all the others who had phoned me, to bring a police car, 'Marica,' to transport the prisoners to the bridge between Mali Zvornik and Zvornik." Mr. Theunens, do you agree that statement reflects what you wrote about the arrest of four persons, including Ulemek, nicknamed Legija?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The thing that is common, that it both concerns an arrest of four men on the 8th of April, but this document doesn't mention names.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement did you refer to the Vuckovic brothers? Vojin Vuckovic and Dusan Vuckovic, twins?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, I referred to the two Vuckovic brothers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to keep matters short. Is there anything in this story which would not fit into the four people arrested as you described it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the reference to military policemen is -- does not correspond with the statement Vojin Vuckovic gave, i.e., it does not correspond with P1190, because he identifies Ulemek as a member of Zeljko Raznjatovic's Volunteer Guard, and I haven't seen any information indicating that Vojin and Dusan -- okay, the twins are not mentioned, but the fourth person, Zoran Rankic, was a former official or was -- has been an official in the Serbian Radical Party War Staff until December 1991. I have not seen information that he was a military policemen, so that's the difference I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are differences, only to a limited extent contradictions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell me -- actually, it says here we will go on doing this, and so on and so forth. Let's not waste any time.
