This witness who's a Muslim and a policeman, he said that he was called by General Jankovic from Tuzla. Do you know who General Jankovic from Tuzla was and what position he held on the 8th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. General Savo Jankovic was the commander of the 17th JNA Corps at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that General Savo Jankovic, commander of the 17th Corps on the 8th of April, when you say the attack on Zvornik started, called the police, asking them to release -- well, there are differences there, but he is saying that it was two military policemen who had obviously gone to Zvornik with his knowledge. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that the document states that General Jankovic stated that these are -- that these were military policemen. I'm reading it again, but I don't see -- I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, let's, again, try to keep matters clear. Are you asking Mr. Theunens to interpret this statement, or are you asking Mr. Theunens whether he has any additional knowledge about a phone call made by General Savo Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I'll put it this way: This witness says that General Jankovic was the commander of the 17th Corps, and on the 8th of April when the attack on Zvornik started, he asked whether it was possible to take these four men out of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does that indicate to you that the commander of the 17th Corps knew on 8th of April that four persons were in Zvornik, that they were arrested? And was he, as commander of the 17th Corps, urging for them to be released?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document states that Jankovic called the witness and asked the witness about the possibility to take the four men out of town. So that implies that he knew about the situation with these four people, four men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Just one more question in relation to that: Do you know who Colonel Boskovic is, from the headquarters in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the Nedeljko Boskovic, but I thought he was a general. And he was, at that moment in time, chief of the security administration. But, again, I'm confused by the rank, because the chief of the security administration should be a general.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, witness. Now I'd like to ask you a question and then we'll see whether it is necessary to deal with some other documents as well. We see that one of these four men was Ulemek, Legija, we saw that you said that one of them was Zoran Rankic from the Serb Radical Party, now I'm interested in the Vuckovic brothers from the Yellow Wasps. Do you have any proof and do you have any indication of these people having any relations whatsoever with the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents I have reviewed do not allow to draw such a conclusion, so they do not indicate any linkage between the Vuckovic brothers and the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. I would now like to ask that we move on to a new topic, and that is Captain Dragan, or, rather, Dragan Vasiljkovic, or Daniel Snedden.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a look at 2D319. Your Honour, since this document is one that I received at the very last moment from the investigator, we only translated the part that we would like to deal with. We are going to provide it to the CLSS so that it can be fully translated. Actually, it has already been given to them by my assistant. So with your leave, I would just like us to have a look at those parts that we had marked, because the document has six pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us when your investigator received the document, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, he sent it to me during the weekend. I really don't know. I can check that as well. I did not check when he obtained the document, but he sent it to me during the weekend. And it's during the weekend that we made an effort, since the CLSS was not working, that we translated parts of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please, at a later stage, provide this information. You want to put -- have it put on the record that you object against using this document without a full translation. Mr. Weber, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: More than that. We object to the use of the document period. We have no notice of it. It was not included even in the very last notification on the 31st of October, 2010. We've received a list of exhibits yesterday just at the start of court; I do not see 2D319 a part of those exhibits. Overall, we've been notified of over 128 documents by the Simatovic Defence in six separate e-mails, so we do not even see this included. So at this time, without even the Prosecution having an opportunity to look at the document, we at least request that it not be used at this time and that we have an opportunity to look at it before further presenting any views on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, what about using it tomorrow morning, which at least leaves some time to the Prosecution and also enables them to consult with language assistants in order to see what the remainder of the [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do thank you for your understanding. And of course it would only be civilised for us to agree with that. After all, that is a constructive proposal. I'm going to leave Captain Dragan for the end of my examination so that the Prosecution can familiarise themselves with that topic. So I am going to move on to yet another topic now, and I'll deal with this one tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, let's have a look at this -- or, actually, do you know the name of Radojica Bozovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What is your view of his position -- or, rather, no. Let me rephrase this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at 2D65.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For the record, the Prosecution received notice of this document on 31st of October, 2010, at 5.44 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this isn't a long document. Please read through it. So have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I've seen that document, but I'm familiar with another document that indicates that at a certain moment in time Radojica Bozovic, also known as Kobas [phoen], holds an assignment in the Doboj CSB, i.e., the police of the Republika Srpska in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So this is yet another document which shows that as of the 13th of January, 1993, the minister of the interior of Republika Srpska, Mico Stanisic, pursuant to the rules governing the internal organisation and work of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska, assigns Mr. Radojica Bozovic to a post; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean by "yet another document." But -- I mean, Radojica Bozovic is one of the individuals - you can see throughout parts 2 and part 3 of the report - who are at one -- in the beginning, active in the training centre in Pajzos. Then subsequently - and I can give you references if you want them - they are identified as members of the Red Berets or even commanders of a Red Beret unit, for example in Doboj. And he's also extensively mentioned in the Pauk diary, which discusses the participation of sub-units of the special-purpose unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia in operations in Western Bosnia. So this is one document that shows an assignment held by Bozovic at one moment in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore you will agree with me that we can see from this document that he was assigned to the post of the commander of a police detachment of a Special Police brigade for Doboj; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness has answered that question already. We've now spent four minute, well over four minutes, to establish what already in the first answer was clear, that Mr. Theunens seems not to disagree that Bozovic was appointed in this position on that date. That took us now four, close to five minutes. Quite not understandable. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you have just said that Mr. Bozovic was also mentioned in the Pauk operation as belonging to a subordinated unit. Let me just check my notes. When you discussed the Pauk operation, you said to my learned friend Mr. Weber that Radojica Bozovic was subordinated to the Pauk command in 1995 and that Pauk was predominantly composed of MUP members. And that's at page 71 of the transcript of the 26th of October of this year?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and he --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What is the basis for your statement that Pauk was composed mostly of MUP members? And which MUP, ultimately?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Pauk command was a mixed structure whereby there were officers of the SVK, part of it, the chief of the Pauk command was an SVK officer, but there were also senior members of the MUP Serbia involved as commanders of sub-units. Radojica Bozovic, also known as Kobas, for example, signs a document as the commander of --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, please, we will come to that. My question was, I think, quite clear and specific. Based on what evidence did you arrive at the conclusion that Pauk was mostly composed of MUP members?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently you start your answer by indicating that there were sub-commanders from the MUP. Mr. Bakrac is interested in the quantitative statement that most members. Could you please focus on that. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- the Prosecution would ask that the witness just be allowed to provide his answers. There's over 30 pages in the report on the Pauk command, so possibly a very open-ended, broad question as it appears on 51, line 20 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did not mind Mr. Bakrac here intervening because the witness - and it's not for the first time - was not yet very focused. Therefore I repeat the question. It is about -- let me phrase that again. It is about mostly composed of MUP members, which I do understand to be more than half. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not made a quantitative analysis of the composition of the Pauk command; but as I stated, the commander of -- or the chief of the Pauk command is an SVK officer. The command of tactical 2 was Legija, a member of MUP Serbia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'll read to you what your testimony was at page 8111: "In the Pauk command which was active in western Bosnia-Herzegovina between November 1994 and August 1995, and as is discussed in the report, Pauk was predominantly manned by members of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia, including members of the special-purpose unit." Did you want to express by "predominantly" that they were not in the majority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honours, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because you say you did not make any quantitative analysis.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honours, I tried to summarise the quantitative aspect as well as the qualitative aspect, i.e., that the number of senior positions or positions I considered serious, senior, like, for example, the commands of tactical groups --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then keep matters short. You did not intend to say that it was by the majority manned in a quantitative way, which Mr. Bakrac may lead you to either rephrase your question or to put another question to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, let's look at Exhibit D47. D47. This is a document of the National Defence of Western Bosnia, Supreme Command. The date is 3 March 1995. Office of the president of Western Bosnia. And subject is a list of military personnel envisaged to be present at the reception. So the first seven are chiefs of the Supreme Command, and then we have, under 7, Mile Novakovic, commander of Pauk. Can you tell us what position did Mile Novakovic have prior to and on the 3rd of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a lieutenant-general in the SVK, and I believe that he was Chief of Staff, so not chief of defence staff but Chief of Staff of the SVK. But not simultaneously with the position he held in Pauk.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, Cedo Bulat, chief of the Pauk command, what was his position before and during this time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it should be Chief of Staff of the Pauk command. And he was the -- I mean, that's also in footnote 407 in part 2 of the report, command of the 21st SVK Corps, Kordun Corps of the SVK. That was the position he held in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Latinovic, chief of logistics of Pauk, did you learn who this individual was and what position he held?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean all that is explained on page 131 of part 2 of the report, where these individuals are clearly identified as SVK officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So the top echelons of the Pauk command were all members of the SVK; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that would only be a partial conclusion; but because the other documents I have included in that section demonstrate that they receive instructions, I cannot state permanently but there are a number of examples indicating that, for example, Novakovic has to speak to Jovica, whereby the last name is not given, or has to go to Belgrade to meet Jovica, indicating to me that senior officials of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia - there's also reference to Frenki -- to a Frenki in the Pauk log-book, D47 - that these officials play a leading role in issuing instructions to the military command of the Pauk command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll be going through two or three documents now and then you'll tell me if you stand by this position of yours. Before we look at the next document, can you tell me if you know how many corps participated in the Pauk operation, and which armies did they come from? Can I be of assistance, did the -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me to look in my report, and I try my best to answer your question. It is my understanding that Pauk involves units, recently-established units, of the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia as well as of the SVK. There is information that they are also units or sub-units of the special-purpose unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, as well as the unit of Slobodan Medic, also known as Boca; this unit is regularly identified as the Skorpions. And overall, Pauk co-ordinated its operations with the units in the -- on the other side of the Bihac pocket of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I apologise if I didn't notice it; did you mention the Army of Republika Srpska? You did. Yes, I can see it now. You said that they co-ordinated, but I'm asking you if units of the Army of Republika Srpska participated in the operation. Perhaps I can refer you to General Milovanovic and his statement, to assist you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I have not seen specific documents on identifying which units of the SVK were -- I'll rephrase that because -- I mean, I try to be very specific. In a sense, I do remember that, for example, units of the SVK would provide fire support, but my recollection is that they did it from the territory they held in Croatia. Now, again - and this is not covered in my report, but - I went to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see whether -- the question was about the Army of the Republika Srpska. Let me just ... and the answer seems to be focusing on --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the Army of the Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please reread the question, whether units of the Army of Republika Srpska participated in the operation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. I recollect that there was co-ordination, as I mentioned earlier, with -- I mean, between the VRS, who were on the western side of the enclave, the Bihac -- enclave of Bihac pocket, with the Pauk command. But I cannot establish whether that was a permanent co-ordination. But I know that during specific operations this co-ordination took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you finished your answer, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm looking at the clock. And I'd only like to spend two minutes on a document, because you mentioned the units belonging to Slobodan Medic, aka Boca, that's to say, Skorpions, as participating in the Pauk operation. Can we call up 2D253. And we'll go back to documents relating to Pauk in the afternoon session. 2D253, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It's a very short document, please read it, and we'll have your comments on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2D253.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It will have been helpful if the two -- I mean, if the stamp in blue had been translated. Maybe it's on the second page; I don't know if there's a second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'll assist you. It's a stamp by the municipality of Palilula of 1999 whereby the authenticity of the photocopy is verified. And we can have its translation on page 2. So, hereby, the municipality of Palilula certifies to the fact that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I think it would take Mr. Theunens approximately two seconds to read what is on the second page. Mr. Theunens, you've seen it it's verification stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we are out of time already. Please tell us, do you have any knowledge about Boca Medic on the 13th of April, 1993, in Djeletovci, together with his unit, was under a military command and part of a military post, or do you have any -- any information to that effect?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this refers to what I stated earlier, that in the territory held by the RSK, between the acceptance of the Vance Plan early 1992 and November 1992, several steps are undertaken to circumvent the demilitarisation and demobilisation stipulations of that Vance Plan by first transforming the TO into PJM; and then subsequently, the PJM, at the latest by November 1992, is transformed into the SVK. And this also applies to the training centre in Erdut, as we saw earlier, as well as -- actually, there was no military installation in Djeletovci. Medic was guarding and participating in the exploitation of the oil fields at Djeletovci, whereby the oil was pumped from Djeletovci towards the refinery in Pancevo in Serbia, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Theunens, one other question, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Bakrac. You said you needed one minute to 12.00, you said you needed two minutes, you've now taken five minutes. We adjourn. And any further questions can be put to Mr. Theunens this afternoon. We resume at 2.30 in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to briefly address one matter, which is the following: Mr. Simatovic, I do understand that there was some confusion about you being transported to the UNDU during this lunch break. This may have been caused by the fact that the Chamber usually does not intervene in any way with transportation. The only reason why the Chamber took up this matter with the Registry was because of the condition of Mr. Stanisic. And for scheduling purposes, we inquired into what time it would take, and we also consulted with Mr. Jordash; that apparently has created an impression that the Chamber was not interested in you being transport to the UNDU, which, of course, was not the case, although we would have left it to the normal routine. Whereas for Mr. Stanisic it requires a bit of separate attention. And that if that confused those responsible for the transportation, that is regrettable, but I was informed that finally the transportation was arranged for. I thought it would be good to explain to you that, why we paid attention to the matter for Mr. Stanisic and not for you, because we had to take into account, for example. And we had to consult with Mr. Jordash on the matter as well. Then, Mr. Bakrac, are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, at the end of the last session we were discussing an issue, and for some reason I was unable to call up that last page of the transcript, but it appears to me that you said that when UNPROFOR came to Slavonia, there followed a demilitarisation and a change in the cadre of the establishment of some of the units; is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I discuss the Vance Plan, because that's what we are talking about, in part 2 of my report, where I explain, okay, the key characteristics of the Vance Plan, and one of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, let's try to keep as focused as possible. I understood the testimony of Mr. Theunens to be that not the character changed but, rather, the names given changed. That's how I understood his testimony. Mr. Theunens, did I understand your testimony well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. That is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We discussed it twice today, indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The practical expression of the changes that occurred, or the practical reflection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So not the character changed, but the names given to the institution changed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if after the Vance Plan there had to follow a demilitarisation, is it not more logical, then, for military names or titles to change into police ones rather than vice-versa?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, a demilitarisation is not so much concerned by names, but it's concerned by the level of mobilisation of forces, as well as the activities of these forces and the location of their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the Vance Plan, the military post in Djeletovci, was it contrary to the provisions you just referred to concerning the storage of weapons and the like?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not addressed this in my report, but for my work in UNPROFOR, my understanding is that Djeletovci was not used as a recognised weapons storage site in that part of Sector East. And when I use the term "recognised weapons storage site," for the implementation of the Vance Plan, a number of weapons storage sites with a so-called dual-key system were established within the territory covered by the UNPAs, the United Nations Protected Areas. And the dual key refers to UNPROFOR as well as the local Serb structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In respect of the base in Djeletovci, did UNPROFOR take any sort of measures?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not aware of any specific measures taken by UNPROFOR in relation to the base in Djeletovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry -- I'm sorry. Just to complete, except for reporting, if there were violations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Mr. Theunens. And, Your Honours, I had to briefly consult my client. Can we now move into private session for a question that was put in direct examination in private session as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, before the break, we spoke of the Pauk operation. I'd like us to look at a document, namely 2D51. It's a document from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska sent to the commands of the 1st and 2nd Corps and the Serbian Army of the Krajina for their information. The dispatch was sent by Deputy Commander Lieutenant-Colonel Manojlo Milovanovic. It was filed with the command of the 1st Krajina Corps in July of 1994. Please look at the document, and I'll draw your attention to two issues. If you wish to read through for the sake of the context, I'll wait. Do you see item 2 there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. It's my impression that this is the same document as P381, which is discussed on page 127 of part 2 of my report. The only difference being that the registration number -- and there may be a typo there, but here it says 02/274. Okay, the slash in my copy has been replaced by a 1. But I think that's just a typo. But it should be the same document. And I see item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Theunens, my apologies. That's perhaps why I omitted to identify the document. But let's look at item 2. It reads: "Pursuant to an agreement between the Army of Yugoslavia, the Army of Republika Srpska, the Serbian Army of Krajina, and the armed forces of Western Bosnia, Directive 6 issued by the Supreme Command of the armed forces of the RS, dated the 11th of November, 1993, the agreement concluded in Vojnic on the 24th of June, 1994, between the representatives of VRS, SVK, and military representatives of Western Bosnia, the VRS had as its task the commencement of offensive actions on the 10th of July, 1994, in the direction of the Una river in order to link up the forces of the 5th Corps of the so-called BH army in order to reach the right bank of the Una and thus take control over the Cazinska Krajina, together with the forces of the Western Bosnia province." My question is, does this concern the Pauk operation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is no direct reference to Pauk even if it concerns the same area of operations. Una 1994 is a predecessor of the operations that were led by the Pauk command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the agreement I referred to just now, among all these sides, did you find among them the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I discussed this document on page 127, 128 of part 2 of my report, and on the next page you see a reference to P1285, which refers to a meeting on I would call the higher level, involving senior representatives of the SVK, VJ, the AP WB, as well as Mr. Slobodan Milosevic and Mr. Jovica Stanisic, to organise military support to Fikret Abdic and the AP WB. And this is how command and control would work. So first there is a political decision-making process; and then, as we see in this specific combat order, the military command levels use the political instruction in order to develop military plans whereby they establish specific missions for specific units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Theunens, if my understanding of what you said to us before the break is correct, you said that the MUP of the Republic of Serbia was involved in the commanding process over these forces; and correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered this question. I mean, this is Una 1994. Una 1994 on the basis of this document does not include any references to the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. It's only when we look at the Pauk documentation that we see clear references to what I would call senior officials of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia and their personnel participating in operations led by the Pauk command. But this is Una 1994; it's something else; it's the predecessor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if I understand you correctly, you said, in support of the statement you've repeated just now, that Mile Novakovic, the commander of the Pauk command, went to Belgrade to see an individual by the name of Jovica. Correct me if I'm wrong. It is on this basis that you draw the conclusion to the effect that the MUP had a commanding role to play in this operation.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just one of the references I used. I also used the SVK security organs report P382, which is discussed on page 133 of part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, now that you're referring to this, can you tell me specifically what was it in that document that led you to conclude that the MUP of Serbia had a commanding role in the Pauk operation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I look at documents in a context. P382 covers a visit by Mr. Jovica Stanisic to the Krajina - if I'm not wrong, it's Petrovac Gora - but it's the -- he visits and he has a meeting with senior officers of the SVK. There is also reference in P382 - and that's on page 134 of part 2 of my report - to a meeting that Mr. Stanisic has with Milan Martic and General Novakovic who -- and I didn't mention that this morning, but who, according to P8 -- 382, was retired at that moment. And this meeting takes place on the 13th of November. And this is, again, what I would call -- it's part of the command and control, but a decision-making process where first political instructions are developed which are subsequently put into action by the units --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And just to finish, okay, there's no doubt that, as I explained in page 131, that there were a number of SVK officers in the Pauk command, but we have seen the document -- one document earlier, the invitation, and we can also look at D47 where there are at least two tactical group commanders who are individuals who, according to other documents, are identified as senior members of the MUP Serbia. And I'm referring that to Milorad Ulemek, also known as Legija, and Kobac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you told us this repeatedly, and it is up Their Honours to adjudicate these facts. It is yours to state them and ours to challenge them. Tactical group is one of a lower-ranking formations; is it not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends of the situation. I mean, I have not been established to see how many forces were involved -- excuse me. I've not been able to establish how many forces were subordinated to the Pauk command. Now, we're talking about a very local conflict; it's only occurring on the front line between the AP WB and the 5th Corps. As far as I understand the situation, the tactical group was the immediate echelon below the command of Pauk. And they were actually conducting the operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if I told you that four or five corps participated in it, what would be -- what sort of formation would a tactical group be then, in view of the strength, a higher level or a lower-level structure?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is a speculative question because you said that four or five corps participated; do you mean the corps in their entirety, or elements of the corps? And if yes, a document that would highlight what elements of the corps would participate would maybe make it easier for me to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I will be guided by your logic and ask you the following: --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not a matter logic. It's a matter of facts. We earlier, as you said, established that -- at least we heard that five corps participated. If I say that a class of pupils participate in a race, then that could be that three out of those pupils participate or the whole of the class; that has not been established. So therefore, it's not a matter of about logic. It's first of all a matter about facts. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I will ask you about facts. The basis on which you conclude that the MUP was in command of the operation was the meeting between Jovica Stanisic, Milan Martic, and General Novakovic. Do you know what exactly was discussed at this meeting? Do you have any facts to that effect?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, if you look at my report, my conclusion is not only based on P382, but also on the diary, as well as other documents that are quoted in the section on Pauk. Now, P382 provides an account of the meeting as provided by Colonel Smiljanic to the chief of the security organs of the SVK, Colonel Rade Raseta, at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please, I don't have time enough to go through the Pauk diary. Can you give me references from that document where we can find the facts based on which you conclude that Jovica Stanisic showed to have a commanding role in the Pauk operation at this particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't written in my report that Mr. Jovica Stanisic has a commanding role in the Pauk operation. However, P382, according to P382, Mr. Stanisic represents the Government of the Republic of Serbia at the Pauk command post. I don't claim that he is there in permanence, because when I then link that information with the information in the Pauk diary, there are entries, for example, footnote 417, an entry for the 19th of November, 8.00 in the morning. It says that Novakovic, OG Pauk, has to go and see Jovica at 11.00. On the 22nd of November, at 1655 - that's footnote 418 - there is an entry indicating that Pauk has to report to Belgrade; he knows to whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So it is on the basis of these two facts that you conclude that the MUP -- well, fine you didn't say that it was Jovica Stanisic who played a commanding role, but that the MUP played a commanding role in Pauk. Is that your evidence now? Command and control --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution just want to put on the record that, for reference, at footnotes 415 through 420, reference specific entries from the Pauk diary.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't use the expression --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That that's -- I do not see what the comment. It's clear that the footnotes refer to the -- because that appears from -- it says entry, entry, entry; and entry is usually used in the context of a log or -- and we see that in 415 - it may perhaps not specifically say ... yes, 416 clearly refers to the operative diary of the Pauk command. So I think it was perfectly clear. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The only reason I brought it up was in response to page 67, the question at line 18, just -- Mr. Bakrac was: "Can you give me references from that document," referring to the Pauk diary, which we can find facts that relate to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it seems that whatever the reason may have been, there's no confusion about that, what these footnotes stand for. Mr. Bakrac, I have one tiny little thing, which is the following: You moved in your questioning from documents showing that Mr. Stanisic played a commanding role during that meeting, and then later you were talking about a commanding role in the operation. Could we please be very accurate in this respect, whether you are talking about the meeting or whether you are talking about the Pauk operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was discussing the meeting. And I wanted Mr. Theunens to tell me what it is on the basis of that meeting that made him conclude that either Jovica Stanisic or the Serbian MUP played a commanding role.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have tried to explain - I can do it for a third time - that I didn't just draw conclusions on one document. The documents have to be considered in context. If you read my report, you will not find any suggestion that Mr. Jovica Stanisic is in command of Operation Pauk on the basis of P382. I mean, another document which shows he's -- the level of interest Mr. Stanisic has for the upcoming operations is P308, where he is reported visiting and meeting General Talic, the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps of the VRS, and where, according to the report that was compiled by security organs of the 1KK, he, i.e., Mr. Jovica Stanisic, had provided -- or he boldly stated that he had provided forces strong enough to ensure the liberation of Velika Kladusa and Fikret Abdic's return there but that he needed to synchronise this task with the forces of the VRS and the SVK. Yeah, there it stands for Supreme Command staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I draw conclusions on the basis of documents, and I look at documents in context, as I have explained in the methodology I have applied. P308 can be found on page 135 of part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please bring up P308. P308, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it, sir, if I understood correctly, I believe you said that Mr. Jovica Stanisic has showed a degree of interest; isn't that a completely different indication from what you say when you based your conclusion that it was Jovica Stanisic or Serbian MUP who had a commanding role in Operation Pauk? Here is P308. Perhaps we can see what it is in that document that makes you conclude anything about Jovica Stanisic's commanding role.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I have not stated in my report that Mr. Jovica Stanisic commanded Pauk. I have given you a few references indicating that the person who holds the military command of Pauk is -- reports to a Jovica, whereby it's my conclusion that it's Jovica -- Mr. Jovica Stanisic, and that there are a number of senior officials of the MUP of Serbia playing a commanding role in the Pauk command as commands of tactical groups. Now, this is not the P308 I'm referring to, unless there's an error in the -- in the P number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think there might be an error in the P number. I'm checking it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologies, Your Honours. I'm ready to drop this document, unless you want to see it particularly. It seems that I've lost quite some time on it, and that was not my original plan. Perhaps later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, that's the Prosecution's fault. I believe it's P380. P380. We will note that -- this and make the corrections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean in the reports by the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The footnote in the report is incorrect. It should be P380, based on the reference in the chart that was filed by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may continue. And since you lost your time as a result of a mistake by the Prosecution, if you would want to spend five or six or seven additional minutes on 380, you are invited to do so. So it's only fair that you are not the -- well, victim is a big word, but at least that you're not having any prejudice from the mistake. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. We will check P380. I focused in my questioning on this footnote, but I will make that check during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we saw that there were two tactical groups, and you say that there was some participation by senior officials of the Serbian MUP in those groups. What made you conclude that? What document did you refer to when you said that there was an involvement of senior officials of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two individual -- I mean the two main individuals I considered are Radojica Bozovic, also known as Kobac, and I've seen documents where he's identified as a colonel. Now, at least in military doctrine, a colonel is a senior officer. Another individual is Milorad Ulemek, also known as -- as Legija. There I don't remember the exact rank, but I based my conclusion or the use of the words senior on the fact that, I mean, the ranks these people held and/or the position during the conduct of operations. So command of a tactical group, in this context, is not a junior officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, are you trying to tell us that in the Serbian state security in 1993 and 1994 there were ranks?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, the people I have mentioned - and there's also others we have seen, Slobodan Medic - is identified -- I mean, they use ranks to identify themselves. Now, whether these ranks applied --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'm asking you, since that was obviously the information you had, did you double-check that information? And can you testify before this Court that in the relevant period of time in 1993, 1994, and 1995, the officials of the Serbian state security service had ranks? Did you try to ascertain that or not? It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to get to the core of the issue. The issue apparently being whether senior MUP officials were playing a role in Operation Pauk. Now, in the report we find that Bozovic was commander of the TG 3 and was involved as such in Pauk, and for Ulemek he is described as commander of the Tactical Group 2; and Mr. Theunens says they both were MUP officials. He explained that by their rank or by their position - and I take it that that's a reference to Tactical Group 2 and 3 - that they could not consider to be anything else than senior officials or senior-ranking officials. Now, whether or not they held certain ranks in the MUP seems not to be the core of the problem. The core of the problem is whether MUP officials played a role at a higher level in commanders of technical groups in Operation Pauk. Now, we can spend another hour on the ranks in the MUP. At this moment - it seems it could be important for other purposes - but for what we are talking about at this moment, the ranks seems not to be of great importance for what apparently is the core of the testimony. Unless you have any specific questions why, despite the fact that, as Mr. Theunens tells us, there were commanders of the Tactical Groups 2 and 3 in Pauk, whether that rank in the MUP would change the picture he had given, unless you have questions for that, I'd like you to again focus on what seems to be the core of this part of the testimony. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, one minute to respond. We dispute the fact that at the time the two persons in question were members of the Serbian DB, during the time relevant to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then apart from ranks, let's then -- if you dispute that, let's -- where Mr. Theunens only qualifies them as MUP officials, apparently you want to demonstrate that - I don't know - whether they were MUP officials or not, but certainly not DB officials. Let's then focus on that issue. That was not clear for me up until this moment, Mr. Bakrac. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Precisely that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I, therefore, have a simple question for you, Mr. Theunens: Did you check whether at that time there were any ranks in the state security service? And I'm referring to the employees of the state security service. Did they have ranks?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as was indicated in the beginning of my testimony, I have not analysed the structure of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, so I'm not able to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Theunens, a moment ago I showed you 2D65. We saw that on the 13th of January, 1993, the minister of the interior of Republika Srpska, Mico Stanisic, issued a decision on the appointment of Radojica Bozovic to the position of the Special Brigade police platoon commander for the area of the Security Services Centre in Doboj. What document do you assert that Radojica Bozovic, in 1994, when he was a member of the tactical group in Operation Pauk, was a member of the Serbian state security service?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not put in my report that Bozovic is, when he is serving is commander of TG 3, is a member of the state security service. The documents I reviewed only allowed to establish that they were officials of the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: On the basis of what document did you ascertain that Radojica Bozovic was an official of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia at that point in time? Let's take this one step at a time. And I mean specifically during Operation Pauk.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I based my conclusion on the positions held prior to Pauk by Mr. Bozovic and I mean throughout the conflict in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, whereby we know that on the basis of P1080 he was in May 1992 in Pajzos. In May -- excuse me. After May 1992, he was in Doboj. P1439 also refers to his presence in Doboj. End of 1992/early 1993, he is reported in Skelani, according to P1441 and P399. And these earlier assignments were again based on the documents I reviewed. In my view, assignments in the MUP of Serbia. I didn't see the document you showed me by Mico Stanisic. Now, it would be a document that would be important to look at in the context of the other documents in order to see whether it was just a regularisation, i.e., to create the impression that Mr. Bozovic was indeed an employee of the MUP of the Republika Srpska, whereas in fact he was still an employee of the MUP of Serbia; or whether, on the other hand, as you tried -- as you suggest, that he was serving full time - if I can say so - exclusively in the MUP of the RS of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, with all due respect, did you work for the Prosecutor until recently - the Prosecutor of this Tribunal - perhaps until last year or two -- until two years ago?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's part of the CV, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, is it possible that -- well, we'll go on to prove that, but let's say, for the sake of the argument, that Radojica Bozovic in 1993 was a member of the Serbian MUP reserve, does that necessarily make us conclude that in 1994, during Operation Pauk, he was a senior or high-ranking official of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would have to look at the specific documents and see whether there are any documents that indicate his transfer from the the MUP --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: His transfer from the MUP Serbia to the MUP RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'm asking you, did you come across a piece of evidence or document which would prove, and I mean a specific written document, proving that Radojica Bozovic was in the Serbian MUP at all, at any time, and especially in 1994 and 1995? And please be specific in your answer because I'm wasting an awful lot of time. We have a some of things to prove, hence I'd like you to be specific.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen a specific document except for --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Oh, sorry. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't really finish my answer, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I haven't -- I mean, it's not reflected in my document -- in my report, at least. I don't remember seeing a specific document indicating the -- whether or not Mr. Bozovic was in 1994 or 1995 a member of the MUP Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Another question concerning Mr. Ulemek, Legija.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to point out there are documents that refer to him being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you are supposed not to comment on the evidence given by the witness. You should refrain from doing that. Is that clear to you? If there's anything, if you want to point out certain documents, you either do it later when submitting argument, or in re-examination you refresh the memory of the witness, but not commenting during the course of the cross-examination; is that clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in 1996, Milorad Ulemek, Legija, was appointed commander of the unit for special operations. Do you have any documents or any piece of evidence that would prove that Milorad Ulemek, Legija, prior to 1996, was a high-ranking official of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name is mentioned, I mean, Milorad Ulemek, or Legija, is mentioned in a number of security or information reports by security organs of the JNA VJ. I'm just trying to locate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, perhaps I can be of assistance. There is a single document in existence that you put forth from the security organs in 1995 where there is a suspicion that Mr. Ulemek, aka Legija, was in any relationship with the state security service, and I believe I showed you that document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will look during the break whether there's other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Theunens. I thank you very much. Let us move on to another two exhibits relating to Pauk.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 2D55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting for that document, for you, Mr. Bakrac, it's the same. It's, I think, appreciated if you ask Mr. Theunens whether it would be of any assistance. You give him the number of the document, but then starting summarising the document is not for counsel to do. It's helpful if you say, Did you want to refer to ... and then you give the name of the document, and then Mr. Theunens will have a look at the document or it will refresh his memory, and then he'll give the answers to the questions. Please proceed. We are looking now at 2D55.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, have a look at this document dated June 24, 1995, the Military Post 9139 Kostanica. "On the 20th of June, 1995, in the AP ZB, active operations were carried out for the successful completion of the task issued by the commander of the Main Staff of the SVK. He commended all members who participated in its completion. We are hereby sending you the full text of the telegram of commendation. "The entire operations group headed by Lieutenant-General Milan Novakovic is commended, signed by Lieutenant-General Milan Mrksic, commander." Did you have occasion to see this document before? And it is an OTP document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I believe this document is -- was included in the CD, or DVD, you gave me earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does this document enable us to conclude anything about the command structure of Operation Pauk?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document confirms that Lieutenant-General Mile Novakovic has the -- there it says "headed," but has the military command over the Pauk operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could we have a brief look at 2D57, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, the document is D70, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is also document with ERN number which we were able to identify from the batch disclosed to us. On the stamp, it says: Republic of Serbian Krajina, Main Staff of the Serbian army. Decision and order on preparations for combat operations. Have a look at item 3, please. "The Pauk command shall carry out preparations to go on to the attack, taking on the TG of the first echelon and bringing them into the attack along the selected axes. In this connection, the Pauk command shall carry out reconnaissance and collect the necessary information about the forces of the 5th Corps and the terrain and forward the information to TG commanders during reconnaissance. The Pauk command shall mobilise all its combat units." Therefore we see that the tactical groups were included. Can we clearly discern from this document who was in command of Operation Pauk? It was signed by commander Lieutenant-General Mrksic. We can see that on the next page.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this document shows that -- I think it's from June 1995. Or is it May? If you go back to the top again of the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document shows that on the 30th of May, 1995, Mile Mrksic, as the command of the SVK, issues orders to ... to -- I mean, to the corps of the SVK, as is mentioned in the first paragraph under "I hereby order." And he also issues instructions to the Pauk command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move on to the next document, which is 2D71. It is dated 9 March 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It is General Mladic's commendation drafted and signed by assistant commander for morale who says: "Commendation of VRS units for successful combat operations. For the admirable courage exhibited by the soldiers, for the professional leadership and command, for determination, heroism, and the results achieved during the combat operations, and the successful smashing of the offence of the 5th Corps of the Muslim army at the proposal of Lieutenant-General Mile Novakovic, SVK commander, I hereby commend, number 1, the Mauzer combat group of the 1st Bijeljina Light Infantry Brigade of the Eastern Bosnian Corps." Have you had occasion to peruse this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's also on the CD you gave me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, here we also see that the Army of Republika Srpska and General Mladic commends for command and control, it seems, in the Pauk operation, in dispersing the 5th Corps and breaking down their offensive; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there's no reference -- there's no specific reference to what you suggest, i.e., that Mladic commends for command and control. It seems in --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe if you rephrase the question, then it's easy for me to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, I'm just reading, but it seems we do not understand this. For the admirable courage exhibited by the soldiers, for the professional command and control ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think what keeps you apart is that Mr. Theunens tells us that there's no specific reference to the Pauk operation. So therefore the appropriate question would be whether there's any reason to believe that this commendation is related to activities deployed in the Pauk Operation. That seems to be the first question. Could you answer that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- either on the basis of the document itself or on the basis of any other knowledge you may or may not have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow me to assist. Under item 3, we can see what was the area. The 5th Corps in the area of Velika Kladusa on the 5th and 6th of March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand your question now. The document seen in context, i.e., time and location, suggests that the units mentioned under command, I mean the numbers 1, 2, and 3, participated in operations in the Velika Kladusa area as part of efforts or combat operations to, what is called smashing the offensive of the 5th ABiH Corps. And a link is made with Lieutenant-General Mile Novakovic, who is identified as SVK commander. I haven't seen in the Pauk diary -- I don't remember seeing in the Pauk diary a clear reference to -- or reference to the units of the VRS, but there were instances where operations were taking place during the time-period Pauk existed on both sides, I would say, of the enclave, whereby units led by or commanded by Pauk were putting pressure on the 5th Corps from the north, and units of the VRS were putting pressure on the 5th Corps from the south. Now, I have no specific knowledge of -- or no knowledge of this specific operation which seems to be referred to here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens, but let me just ask you, as you made reference to this in your report, the combat group Mauzer, what did you find about them? Where did they belong? Whose members were they, and where were they from?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this document, they are identified as a sub-unit of the 1st Bijeljina Light Infantry Brigade of the Eastern Bosnian Corps, the VRS. Now, Mauzer was mentioned, or a person with the nickname Mauzer was mentioned, in relation to take-over operations. I'm not sure anymore whether it was Bijeljina or Bosanski Samac. I mean in the spring 1992. It was actually Brcko; and Ljubisa Sabac is his real name. But there is, at least, a Mauzer with -- I mean, whose real name was Ljubisa Sabac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mentioned re-subordination, but what I can read here in the original document is the Mauzer combat group of the 1st Bijeljina Light Infantry Brigade. So as I understand the document, they were part of the composition of the 1st Bijeljina Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It may be a translation issue. I don't think that anything that you just said contradicts what Mr. Theunens said. So therefore I did not hear of any re-subordination. It's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, in the document mentioning this, Mauzer is D83, which is discussed on page 93 of part 3 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, would you make a connection between Mauzer and his group and the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just going through the report, whether I have any reference on that. No, I cannot identify such a reference of any connections between Mauzer's -- of Mauzer and his group and the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. I don't remember seeing a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would move to another subject, that is to say, another personality. I see that we have two or three minutes remaining until the break, but maybe this would be a good moment to begin the break, a bit earlier than usual, because I am about to move to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then have a break now, and we'll resume at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'd like to discuss a different topic now, namely an individual by the name of Zivojin Ivanovic. You referred to him in your report. Do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed I refer to a Zivojin Ivanovic, also known a Crnogorac. And I have referred to P -- I mean, more specifically, to P569 and to P1085 to discuss his role.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We'll get back to the two documents you relied upon. First I'd like us to look at other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's first look at a Prosecution document, P1085.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And I believe you reference it in report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call it up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is this the document you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, that's the document I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, look at the heading. It reads: SAO Semberija and Majevica, special-purpose unit Brcko, 9 July 1992. This is a certificate confirming that one Joco Stevanovic, a member of the special-purpose unit ... this is a certificate confirming his membership, that is. So commander is Zivojin Ivanovic. Can we conclude on the basis of this document that commander Zivojin Ivanovic was a member of the special-purpose unit of the SAO Semberija and Majevica headquartered in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at this document in isolation, I would agree with you; but - and, again, in my report, this is discussed part 3, page 95. Another document, P569, is a certificate Zivojin Ivanovic signs as commander of the unit for special purposes of the MUP of Serbia. There's also a P1083 that links a Zika Crnogorac, and based on the different nicknames I conclude that this is the same person as Zivojin Ivanovic, linking Ivanovic to the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. Whereby P1083 is even more specific, talking about the state security police of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the Registrar took care that the document will not be shown to the public. It would have been appropriate that you mentioned this, or at least that it was a confidential document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon, Your Honour. I wasn't paying attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, let's look at 2D313. Mr. Theunens, it is my suggestion that Zivojin Ivanovic, the -- is the individual we see on this photograph, and that he, Zika Crnogorac, had the official identity paper indicating that he was a member of the republican secretariat of the interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina as of the 1st of February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that is what this document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In order for us to round off this topic, I'd like to show you several other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 2D301, please. I can see that Mr. Weber is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He is on his feet. Yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to 2D313, I see it as a colour photocopy. If the Simatovic Defence has the ability to produce the original, the Prosecution would request it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we do not keep the originals with us. I will try to provide the Prosecution with the original of this document in due time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we saw the Brcko document dated the 9th of July, 1992. Now this is a document dated the 15th of May, 1993. The command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, on the 15th of May, 1993, in Bratunac, re-subordinated special units of the MUP to the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. Order: "In order to solve the newly-arisen problems in the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade and based on the instructions from the command of the DK," there follows the number, "and pursuant to the order by the commander of the VRS dated 13 May 1993, I hereby order the Republika Srpska special-purpose unit of the MUP under the command of Zivojin Ivanovic, aka Zika Crnogorac, to be re-subordinated to the command of the Bratunac Light Brigade." Is this the one -- one and the same Zivojin Ivanovic whom you claim was the member of -- a member of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document talks about the same person, but it's not my claim. I mean, I refer to P1061 and also, and more specifically, P569, whereby P569 is a certificate which is signed by Zivojin Ivanovic. And the text states that he signed as the command of the unit for special purposes of the MUP Serbia. This is footnote 307 of part 1 of the report, page 110. So what we can see is that Mr. Ivanovic, throughout the conflict, occupies different positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He goes from MUP Serbia to what appears in the previous document, MUP RS. And maybe afterwards he returns to MUP Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Let's look at two documents now. They also come from a collection of Prosecution documents. I don't know if you've had an opportunity to look at them before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's first look at document -- let's chronologically look at 65 ter 4814 first.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I assume you have had an opportunity to look at this document before. We have the heading read: Republic of Serbia, Ministry of the Interior, State Security Department, RDB Centre Novi Sad. About conversations which took place between the 5th and the 16th of November, 1992, and it is on the 17th of November, 1992, that this particular officer filed his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could this document not be broadcast to the public due to the pending protective measures request.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I presume that the next document I will be showing will also require the same precautions, so let's bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let's look at page 3 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record, the instruction is not to show it to the public. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's page 3 in English, the bottom of the page. The paragraph starting with the words "on the 12th of November."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you see the paragraph? It reads:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have the redaction of the operative's name that was just mentioned on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, on from the source till thus. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it was on the CD you gave me prior to the weekend, but I have no other recollection of having seen the document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this particular document from the OTP collection, where the state security department monitors Kajmak, also speaks of Zivojin Ivanovic as a member of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the -- Mr. Bakrac please repeat the last part of his sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Does this document indicate that the state security department in the Kajmak operation monitoring a certain individual showed that Zivojin Ivanovic is a member of the DB of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't show that. A presumption is made, but a presumption is like a presumption; it's not a confirmation. And, again, I refer to P569 and P1061, which indicate a relation, professional relation, between Zika or Zivojin Ivanovic, also known at Crnogorac, and the MUP of Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, there is a document you're referring to, and in the continuation of our case we will be referring to the source of that document. At any rate, I will be showing you Prosecution documents which you haven't seen or haven't been shown and which may lead you to draw a different conclusion.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not so much a matter, I think, of documents I haven't been shown. It may be that these documents became available to the OTP after the report was finished and filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's look at another report which is not to be broadcast to the public either. This is 65 ter 4812, dated the 4th of January, 1993. Again the heading reads: "The Republic of Serbia, Ministry of the Interior, State Security Department, RDB Centre, Novi Sad." I've already stated the date. State secret, extremism. Let's look at page 3 in B/C/S and page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The paragraph should start with the following words: "According to our source ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's page 2 in English, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It's paragraph 2 on this page: "According to our source, on 26 December 1992, Kajmak received information from Zivojin Ivanovic, a Krajina DB member, that he was leaving for Kosovo. Kajmak told him that he had transferred 54 million to his account and added that Ivanovic would have to find a cunning way to withdraw the money." So this isn't an assumption; it is stated that Ivanovic was a member of the DB Krajina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what this document states. And if we then apply the methodology that I have explained earlier during my testimony, we compare these different documents and again we apply the process - reliability of the source, credibility of the information - and we see that there is a contradiction, unless there is deliberate confusion created about the professional allegiance of Zivojin Ivanovic. Which, again, in the context of the issues we are discussing, i.e., there was a high degree of secrecy in relation to the participation of members of the MUP Serbia in the conflict in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, I mean, an attempt to create confusion or deception would not be unusual in that context.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I am putting it to you that this is a TKTR source, in other words, wire-tapping a conversation over the phone. It was listed as state secret and extremism. Can you tell me, what would be the reason for a member of the DB centre of Novi Sad to submit a report to his superiors and make the whole story surrounding Zivojin Ivanovic, a member of that same DB, muddy and foggy? What would be the reason for doing so by using a telephone conversation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, the document doesn't look like a transcript of a telephone conversation, at least the page I have in front of me. And to answer your question, I don't state that it's the member of the DB Novi Sad, DB centre Novi Sad, who is deliberately trying to create a foggy picture, but that it's Ivanovic and his superiors within the MUP Serbia who are doing so. And it would not be unusual that then lower-level members of the DB would not be fully aware of the reality. And just to finish --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and just to finish --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's just -- do you know any specific reasons, or are we just guessing on what the reasons might be on the basis of your experience?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know any specific reasons, but I find it surprising that the document states a Krajina DB member where I don't remember seeing any documents within the OTP collections that link Zivojin Ivanovic to the DB Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
