utterances.text: Could we cut it short. The information is as reliable as the source in this respect is? Could be low, could be high, not knowing who the source is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, even as we discussed earlier, a reliable source can provide information of low credibility and vice-versa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore I said reliable in this respect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I do understand that there's no -- there's not any other documentary evidence which would confirm Zivojin Ivanovic to be a Krajina DB member?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Based on my recollection; yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I've shown you an identity paper and an order earlier on. This is some new evidence that you haven't seen before. Just look at where the -- it is written TKTR source. And do you know what this acronym stands for? It's on page 1 of the document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You just explained it has to do with information collected through the interception of telephone communication; monitoring of telephone calls it says in the document, so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Let's discuss another individual now who you tie in with the MUP of Serbia in your report in this time-period. This is Vasa or Vasilije Mijovic; do you remember him?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. I have -- I mean, there is information, P - I think - 1061, that links him to the special-purpose unit of the MUP Serbia, and then there are other documents, P1083 and P1081, that mention -- that identify him as commander of a Red Berets unit in the Bratunac area after May 1992. And I've also seen a document, P1084, that's from July 1995, that identifies him as the commander of the JATD of the Republic of Serbia. And on the CD you gave me, there was 2D269, where I think there was a kind of a -- not a personnel file, but it seems to be a file of an investigation, where a number of documents were included that provide information on the different assignments Mr. Mijovic held between the 1991 and 1995 time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could you now have a look at the first document that you referred to; that's 1061. That's the unsigned document of the security organ. Which provides a report on --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have a look at 2D315.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The heading says: "Special-purpose unit, Republic of Serbian Krajina, Krajina MUP, Ilok, 19th July 1992." Order: "Whereby it is ordered that the deputy commander, Vasilije Mijovic travels on official business to visit a part of our combat units which carries out combat operations in the territory of the Trebinje municipality." And then the use of an official vehicle is approved, and it is signed by the commander of the unit Zivojin Ivanovic. Is it correct that it follows from this order that on the 19th of July, 1992, Zivojin Ivanovic was the deputy commander of the special-purposes unit of the Republic of Serbian Krajina? I mean that Mijovic was the deputy of Zivojin Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what this document states. And, again, looking at the context, we see that the same individuals are, according to the documents, apparently affiliated to different Serb MUPs. Based on my research, they all start as MUP Republic of Serbia; then some of them are identified as members - apparently, here, now - Krajina RSK MUP; and then we see them appear again in the MUP RS. And it's interesting to follow their career path between the 1991 and 1995 time-period. Just to finish, I would also like to mention that it's quite remarkable that a unit of the Krajina MUP RSK would participate in fighting in the Trebinje area which is located in south-eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina. In order to travel to Trebinje, he would have to travel via Serbia, because you couldn't move directly from Ilok to Bosnia-Herzegovina, at least not over land.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Why was it not possible to travel overland from Ilok to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean without going through Bosnia -- excuse me, without going through Serbia. Then he would have to cross Croatian territory, and I don't think that would have been possible, since when you look at the limit of Sector East on the -- call it on western, the southwestern side there were Croatian forces, and I don't think they would have allowed a member of -- call it the Krajina MUP or the MUP Serbia to cross over the territory of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can we now please have a look at another document. This one was dated the 19th of July, 1992. And the other document is 2D296, dating from February 1993. Mr. Theunens, we see here that it's the command of the 1st Bratunac Brigade. The date is the 21st of February, 1993. Engagement of soldiers of the Republika Srpska special-purpose unit in Bratunac to the special-purpose unit and addressed to Major Mijovic. "Order," it says. This document is an order by which, as far as I understand, the command of the Bratunac Brigade issues a task to the special-purpose unit and practically re-subordinates it. Is this also the way that you understand this document? And I have in mind Republika Srpska when I'm saying all this.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed that is what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. I would now return to a document for which you suggested that it was a document on the basis of which you draw a conclusion -- it is one of such documents from which you draw a conclusion that this person was a member of the MUP of Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see P1081.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Because this is the one you referred to. And I will ask you to show me where exactly one can see in this document that -- that this is a member of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. I would rather say that the document seems to show that the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade re-subordinates the special-purpose unit of the MUP to the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and this is in accordance with the previous document which I presented to you; therefore, I cannot see in this document that there is a connection with the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree you if you look at this document in isolation. But as I explained earlier, the document has to be seen in the context of other documents, for example, P1083, as well as P1084. And, again, 2D269 on the CD you provided me, I have a recollection that on the English page 14, there is an entry in a table stating that Vasilije Mijovic has been sent to Bratunac by the RDB. And my understanding was that this 2D269 actually refers to the RDB of the Republic of Serbia and would then be -- would then corroborate P1061, the unsigned security organ's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let us have a look at the first document which you referred to in your answer to my question. Let us look at it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's P1083.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So can you please show to me in this document -- so can you please tell me, on the basis of this document, where is the source for the notion following from this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please specifically focus on the last big paragraph in this document. And for this purpose, could we please show the next page on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I hope that you will agree with me that there is no source here, there is no trace. What was the basis and source on the basis of which someone drafted this report? Who was questioned by the person, who drafted this report, or which documents he reviewed in order to obtain this particular information?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that there's a specific requirement to include source references or footnotes in such a report. It's a report compiled by the chief of the public security centre in Bijeljina, 29th of June, 2004. And he provides information. What is interesting, that is, information provided in 2004, is --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- is consistent, I mean -- consistent -- corroborates information provided in P1061.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please focus. I think you are making a being mistake. This is not a report written by the chief of the security centre, but I believe that it is addressed to him, to the chief of the security centre Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We should look at the last page to see whether we see a signature then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, can we please see page 2. It just says: "drafted by Dejan Joksimovic." Can we now please have a look -- report drafted by Dejan Joksimovic. Can we please have a look at the first page so we can see who this was addressed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It is addressed, as far as I can see, to the chief of public security centre in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to check that because -- yeah, my understanding is that it's drafted by him, but I would have to check, I mean, if -- I can stand corrected if -- I would have to check what the position was of Dejan Maksimovic [sic] at the time he signed the report. Excuse me, Dejan Joksimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Theunens, I just wanted to compare the documents from which you drew your conclusions with the documents that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have a look at 2D299.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for my understanding, do I understand well that apart from to whom it was addressed, that it originated apparently from that same service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours. So if an error was made, the error would have been that I identified the person who signed the report as the chief of the public security centre in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because the letterhead on which the information is written down is the public security centre of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, but it was an error. And I wanted to clarify this with Mr. Theunens so that we could see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought that instead of dealing with all these details that the main point you apparently wanted to make is that the source of the information on page 2 is not specified, is that -- so that whatever the document says, that you say, It's difficult to verify because you don't know who gave this information?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. That's it precisely. I'm comparing the document on the basis of which the report was drafted, and I'm presenting my own documents which show where these persons belong to Mr. Theunens. Here is 2D299. It is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe just to clarify my answer to the previous question. It's not an academic study where you would indeed look for source references and check the reliability and the level of these source references. It could well be that there is an issue of source protection which is not unusual in the context of such reports and that therefore the specific sources for the specific elements of information were not identified as such in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Theunens, there may be many reasons. You just mentioned one of them. The fact is, what is stated in this information and that we do not have the identity of the source available to us. What that means, in terms of reliability, what that means in the context of the whole of the evidence is still to be seen. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, please have a look at this document. It was signed by commander Vasilije Mijovic. The heading says: "Special unit for special purposes of Republika Srpska, Bratunac, the 19th of April, 1993." And it says: "By an order of the commander at the special unit, the following soldiers are discharged from this unit." And then it's listed who these soldiers are because of conduct unbecoming to a soldier. We can see that there is a signature by Colonel Vukusic who is the commander from the Bratunac military post. Can we conclude on the basis of this document that this special-purposes unit of Republika Srpska was in Bratunac in the month of April 1993 and that it was re-subordinated to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the document deals with the issues of the removal of soldiers. But, I mean, according to the document, Vasilije Mijovic signs as the commander of a special MUP unit of the Republika Srpska on that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Can we now please have a look at the next document. This one is a document dating from April 1993, and the following document dates from the month of May 1993. It is 2D300, drafted by the commander of the 1st Light Infantry Brigade in Bratunac. Cvjetin Vuksic, which states the opinion on the work and activities of commander Vasilije Mijovic. Please have a look at this document first.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the question could be raised, Where did commander -- I mean the first two lines. Where did commander Vasilije Mijovic, when he arrived in Bratunac on the 16 January 1993, together with a company of Special Forces, where did he come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I have shown you some documents from July 1992 which show that Vasilije Mijovic had been in Ilok as a member of the special-purpose unit of the MUP of Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 2D315.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I believe you recall the document. And moving on in a chronological order, trying to indicate the movements of Mr. Mijovic.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that document. And my understanding of the reference to Ilok is the reference to the trading centre in Pajzos where, according to various reports we have seen, members of the MUP Serbia were involved in training, at least during the latter half of 1991, were involved in training Serbian volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I have to waste yet more time and go back to 2D315 to ask you to indicate for us where Pajzos is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not mentioned. That's clearly what Mr. Theunens said. He understands the reference to Ilok as ... So it doesn't mention that. Mr. Theunens gives his interpretation. Now, the issue raised here might be an interesting one. What we see is the special unit of the -- of the, as you indicated, he came from -- he was the Krajina -- let me just check whether it was the Krajina special-purpose unit of the Krajina MUP, I think it was, travelling to Trebinje, which is in a totally different part of the country. Mr. Theunens raised the question what the Krajina MUP special unit would do in Trebinje, which is at a long distance and totally out of the territorial scope of where you would expect such a unit. And I think the same matter now appears here to some extent; someone coming with his unit to Bratunac. And your suggestion was that we would learn from the previous documents where he came from, which does not yet explain why such a unit would travel both to Trebinje, where they are supposed to be engaged in combat activities, and now to Bratunac. Are you going to -- this puzzle which Mr. Theunens more or less put on our table, is it your information to clarify this issue at any moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, should I fail, I merely wanted to get a comment from Mr. Theunens. I don't have it at hand, but I can show you later on that there was an agreement published in the Official Gazette between Republika Srpska Krajina and the RS on co-operation in all aspects of military and police co-operation. Unfortunately, I don't have it here, but I might be able to show it to you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It might clarify matters. Mr. Theunens, are you aware of such an agreement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know of a political agreement called the Prijedor Agreement; I think it's from the latter half of 1992. But I would have to look in my report what it exactly concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that what you were referring to as well, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't dare say anything in advance. I will have to check first when the agreement was signed and published in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because we now see Mr. Mijovic travelling around at various places in the Republika Srpska and you say this could be explained, perhaps, by agreement. It might assist the Chamber to have a look at that agreement sooner or later. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let's look at 2D284 next, which is ... Here we see assistant commander Colonel Milutin Skocajic, from the Drina Corps command, re-subordinates the MUP special-purposes unit under the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. It seems that it is Vasilije Mijovic's unit.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed that is stated in paragraph 1 where the unit is identified as a MUP special-purposes unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at another June 1993 document. It is a dispatch of the Drina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 2D303. 2D303.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, here the command of the Drina Corps, in late June or even in early July 1993, ordered that the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade should immediately prepare his reconnaissance and sabotage unit commanded by Mijovic to be ready to carry out the ordered tasks. Can we clearly conclude, on the basis of this order, that the reconnaissance and sabotage unit - and we saw already how it was transformed from the special-purpose unit to the reconnaissance and sabotage unit - does it enable us to see whether, in June 1993, it was commanded by the Drina Corps, or, rather, the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least, I mean, for a number of tasks identified in the document, upcoming tasks, I mean, the -- the unit of Mijovic is identified as a reconnaissance and sabotage unit. And according to this document, this reconnaissance and sabotage unit, under the command of Mijovic, is part of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. While we are on the topic of the Bratunac Brigade, I'd like us to have a look at some documents concerning Radivoje Tesic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Borivoje Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we -- could I seek some clarification. What -- what I see is that in your questions you very much focus on where in this case the unit under the command of Mijovic appears and under whose command they then are engaged in operations or operational activity. Now, Mr. Theunens raised the question a couple of times that the -- an interesting question is where they came from. You said, Well, it will show that it has to be in with the special unit of the Krajina MUP, but Mr. Theunens also said, in 2D269, you can see that they were sent by the RDB. I'd like to have a look to complete the picture at that document and understand what Mr. Theunens meant and to show us what is in that document that gives the clue he refers to. Could we have -- Yes, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. 2D269 talks about the individual --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... let's -- let's -- let's look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Yep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We haven't seen -- we haven't had it on our screen yet, did we? 2D269. You said it was a report which --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's 42 pages; it's a kind of a file on Vasilije Mijovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's what you indicated earlier. Could you take us to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that part in the document which sheds some light on what you -- to which you refer to earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's English page 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this a --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, out of caution, this is a personnel file that relates to RFA -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and not to be shown to the public. Not to the shown to the public. You said page --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 14, Your Honours. One, four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 14. Could we have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us exactly what you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this -- the page 14, there is a kind of a table, I think. I also notice that -- again, I haven't written down all the references, but in some documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's have a look. Page 14 is no table, as far as I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Is this page 14?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is page 14 of 2D01-1029. Whether that's the document 2D269, I do not know, but.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, I touched the screen again. But it's a -- it's on the table -- it's at the bottom, the information I'm looking for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It says: "We have information that Stevanovic knows Mijovic from the territory of Bratunac, when Mijovic was sent there by the RDB, via Rade Rakonjac from Belgrade." And my conclusion there was that Mijovic was sent by the RDB of the Republic of Serbia to Bratunac. I have also noticed that in some of the translations the Republic of Serbia, Republika Srbija, is translated as -- sorry, Republika Srbija, i.e., the Republic of Serbia, is translated as Republika Srpska, which is confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, is it originally an English document, because then Republic of Serbia would be confusing if you translate it as Republika Srpska. If, however, the original says Republika Srpska, then of course it would be just the opposite, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, I mis -- sorry, I misexpressed myself. It was that Republika Srbija is translated into Republika Srpska. So from Serbian to English translated in something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say this is a document in which you find a reference of Mr. Mijovic being sent by the RDB to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it's part of the picture. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps this may be an issue of translation. In the Serbian original version, I don't see in the last sentence whether it refers to Stevanovic or Mijovic in the Serbian language. Reading from the Serbian version, it seems to me that it refers to Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- that should be verified. The English is perfectly clear in -- knows Mijovic from the territory of Bratunac, when Mijovic was sent there by the RDB. If that is a wrong translation, then that's an important thing to be corrected because that's apparently the basis on which Mr. Theunens tells us that Mijovic might have been sent by the RDB. If not, then Mr. Stevanovic would have been sent there by the RDB. Could we try to verify this over the next break. You certainly have people, and it's just two or three words. Mr. Weber, I take it that you will also have an opportunity to verify the translation in respect of who was sent by the RDB to Bratunac. Please proceed, Mr. -- And I'm looking at the clock. I think it would be time for a break. And we would then, after the break, have another 17 minutes available.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just one second. The Prijedor declaration -- I mean, when we talk about the co-operation between the RS, or the Bosnian Serbs, and the Krajina Serbs, it is P1275, but it doesn't deal with details like police or military co-operation, the Prijedor declaration from 31st October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. And we'll have a break. And we resume at ten minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, have the parties made an effort in order to verify the translation about who was sent it to Bratunac, Mr. Stevanovic or Mr. Mijovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution sees that the document, the translation provided, appears to be through CLSS. We did talk to a language assistant over the break and had a relatively quick translation provided of the sentence. The translation that we were provided says: "We have information that Stevanovic has been connected to Mijovic since the period when he, using a pronoun, stayed in the area of Bratunac as ordered by the RDB and which was done through mediation of Rade Rakonjac from Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means it's not entirely clear who the "he" is; is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That was the understanding of also the language assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This accurately, we believe, reflects the Serbian original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, this document, it's not in evidence; nevertheless, Mr. Theunens relied on it. Mr. Theunens, was this among the documents you were provided with by ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this is one of the documents on the CD, and -- I was provided before the weekend. And I didn't reply on this document for my report. In my report, I relied on the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- I mentioned earlier. But this document, I mean, the translation I had in front of me, corroborated what was, for example, mentioned in P10 - is it now 61 or 60? - I forgot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you briefly describe what the document is about. You said it was a larger document. What is the gist of the -- is it one document, is it ... because this seems to be a two-page part of the document. Is it a collection? Could you give us ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 2D269 in -- on the CD, is a -- the scanned version of a folder with, on the cover page, the name Vasilije Mijovic, and then there are 42 page consisting of different documents which in majority consists of information reports on Vasilije Mijovic. But I believe also there are documents, for example, indicating that he received a beret. There's also documents - if I'm not wrong, because there were many documents on the CD - related to weapons permits, or that he received a weapon, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, is the document new for the Prosecution, or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. And I'll be cautious, and I can provide information if the Chamber would like me to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do we -- we do it in public session?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution received the document that is before you pursuant to RFA 1382 from the Republic of Serbia. It is Vasilije, Vaso, Mijovic's DB JSO personnel file, consisting of the 40-plus pages that are before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, we spent a lot of time on whether he was related to the MUP, yes or no, whether he was reserve, which is something you suggested, Mr. Bakrac. Wouldn't it be the best to have this material available and to have it in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is a Prosecution document, and I believe they would seek to tender it. But in any case, as Mr. Theunens said, it's a voluminous document of 40-plus pages, and I left it for the end, although I've made very little use of it. In any case, I see no problem of having that admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We have no objection to having it admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any party soliciting to tender it or otherwise, or should the Chamber call for it to be produced?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution, at this time, tenders 2D269 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01585.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, in the absence of any objections, is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- sorry, if you allow me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were a number of documents, and I believe also in this one, where I said earlier where the original said "MUP Serbia," where it was translated into "MUP Republika Srbija," so I would be cautious --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- with the translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, have you made paid attention to that comment already?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We're having that checked, based on the witness's comment in the last section. What is a way of proceeding, we can send it out to CLSS to just confirm what the actual translation is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Most specifically on those matters. And then also specifically on what is found on what appears to be page 14, I think it was. Yes, 14 in e-court out of 42. Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, before the break, I asked you whether the name of Lieutenant-Colonel Borivoje Tesic rings a bell.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed he does, Your Honours. He was a battalion commander in 1991 in the guards motorised brigade. And during the operations of OG South in the Vukovar area, he was the commander of an assault attachment, if I'm not wrong, which consisted of forces of his battalion as well as Serbian volunteers. And I've also seen the document indicating this is -- yeah, there's no P number in my report, but on -- on -- in this third part on page 109 where he's identified as the commander -- no, as an officer who is serving, I'm sorry, in the Bratunac Brigade command on 27 of November, 1992. And just to be complete, when I say "guards motorised brigade," it is the guards motorised brigade of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. You provided me with more information than I expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 2D285 next.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I apologise for my previous remark. I'm not trying to sound ironic; I just wanted to say that I wanted to follow the topic of the Bratunac Brigade and, hence, the information you provided assisted me. This is a document of the command of the Bratunac Brigade, dated the 25th of November, 1992. It is a report for that day, submitted to the Drina Corps command. Have a look at items 5 and 6. First of all, perhaps you can explain something to me. It says: "The billeting party from Vukovar was here yesterday. They are arriving on the 26th, 27th, and 28th November, 1992. I kindly ask that you plan the forthcoming mission from 2 December 1992 onwards because of the preparations I have to make together with them." Can you enlighten us? Can you explain what this billeting party from Vukovar is?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, my understanding is that this is a group of people coming from Vukovar to prepare the arrival of volunteers, Serbian volunteers from Vukovar, in order to become a member of the unit of Lieutenant-Colonel Borivoje Tesic, who, not withstanding that he was a VJ officer, at that moment is participating in the combat activities on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a member of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Let's look at item 6 next. "I also kindly ask that you use your authority to help the 7th Novi Sad Company from Brcko Military Post 7410/7 to come to this area, because if they are not allowed to come, they will leave that part of the front of their own accord." Then it says that your influence could be used to ensure and enable further work. In your research, did you come across this 7th Novi Sad Company from that particular military post; and if so, can you tell us what it's about?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar, Your Honours, with one additional document; it's the one on page 109, part 3 of my report, which mentions this volunteers company. I would have to check the VP number again to see what kind of unit is specified in Brcko. Brcko was under Serbian control at the time. There's also information that there was a training centre used by individuals or units known as Red Berets. I mean, you can find it in the Brcko section. But I would have to check the VP number in order to find out which location in Brcko these people who, based on the name, originate from Novi Sad in Serbia, in which location they are normally based.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can we please have a look at the next document, which is 2D288. It's a dispatch from Borivoje Tesic. This one was dated the 25th of November, 1992, and this one was sent on two days later, the 27th of November, 1992. It's short, and I will read it to you: "On several occasions I addressed you to send more personnel from the previously mentioned 7th Novi Sad Volunteers Company but" --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I think that out of an abundance of caution perhaps this document should not be broadcast. And perhaps we should even move to a private session because our next witness is mentioned here, and I'm not sure if any protective measures will be applied to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I wish to deal with a part of your report which has to do with Bosanski Samac. Please have a look at this document. And let us first say whether it is correct that in the night between the 16th and the 17th of April, 1992, there was combat in and around Bosanski Samac and that Bosanski Samac was captured by the 17th Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, just to be more precise, the document states that the -- that "all vital facilities in Bosanski Samac were captured by forces of Tactical Group 17, units of the Serb Territorial Defence, and the police." That's my understanding. I quoted that document on page 76 of part 3 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, they say in the report that the forces of Tactical Group 17, units of the Serb Territorial Defence, and the police participated in this attack. Would you agree with me that this document reflects that these were the units of the local Territorial Defence and local police in addition to this Tactical Group 17?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says Srpska TO. Okay, I pushed -- and milicija. I have no reason to doubt about what you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have a look at Prosecution document P1413. And before I open the document, I have to say that the Prosecution made an error, I'm certain unintentionally, when the document was downloaded, and as a result of this, the pages are mixed. So page 2 is first, and it is followed by page 1. So we should first have a look at page number 2 which is actually page 1 of this document. And this is page number 2 in e-court. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, please have a look at this. The document is dated the 7th of May. The command of the 17th Tactical Group, which we have mentioned, issues an order for combat on the 7th May, 1992, to the Lugar command. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am, because this document is also mentioned -- I mean, it's also mentioned on page 76 of part 3 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the Lugar command refers to a person called Slobodan Miljkovic, aka Lugar, who was a member of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document indeed refers to a -- I mean, Lugar. I've seen Lugar associated with Slobodan Miljkovic. I'm not sure whether in my report I established that he was a member of the SRS, but I have no reason to doubt about what you state. I have no reason to doubt about it. Because I know - sorry to be a bit confusing, but I'm reading my report at the same time - P1422 refers on -- refers to the participation of SRS volunteers in the take-over of Bosanski Samac, so I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Let us now have a look at the third page of this document. It is also, once again, the command of the Tactical Group 17 which issues an order for combat to the Leva Kolona, which is left column command. And please focus on item 2 which says that the commander of this left column would be a man named Crni. Would you agree with me that this Crni refers to Dragan Djordjevic, who was also known by his nickname Crni?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And that's also how I have discussed him, for example, on page 78 of part 3 of my report, referring, for example, to P1417, which is his interrogation by the Banja Luka Military Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Theunens, we will get to that. I'm just moving step by step. Can we see from these two documents that both Lugar and Crni were under the command of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, indeed at the time indicated for these -- I mean for these orders, and the operations that are ordered by these orders, indeed tactical -- the Lugar Group and the Crni Group, or the Leva Kolona, as you called the latter, are subordinated to Tactical Group 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Let us now have a look at P1419 as well. It is a document dated the 3rd of July, 1992, and it is a regular combat report. I'm only interested in the person who signed it; it was the Chief of Staff of the Posavina Brigade, Major Srecko Radovanovic. Is it the Srecko Radovanovic, also known as Debeli, and also a member of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that is my conclusion also on the basis of P1399 discussed on page 79 of part 3 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: He was also a member of a brigade, the Posavina Brigade, of the Army of Republika Srpska; correct? He was the Chief of Staff there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment in time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let us now please have a look at another Prosecution document, P1427. While the document shows up on the screen, I will tell you or, rather, remind you what that is about. It is a judgement of a military court in Banja Luka dated the 6th of February, 1993, against the Accused Djordjevic, Dragan, aka Crni; Miljkovic, Slobodan, aka Lugar; and eight other persons. It is not necessary to mention the names of all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have a look at the end of page 2 in B/C/S, which is the end -- or, rather, the beginning of page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, the document is under seal, and it's not being broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, have a look at this. Under item 10, it says: "All the accused are members of the Army of Republika Srpska." Is that what the document states?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can answer that question. That's what the document states, Mr. Bakrac. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, before passing a judgement, should a military court in Banja Luka or any other court establish clearly and undoubtedly whether the accused are members of a certain organisation? Would you agree with that? And that this is of importance for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I can answer that question as well. Isn't it? Because if you say it is in a judgement, then you should verify whether it's true or not, unless it's just part of the indictment. But you can spend 15 minutes on discussing that. Mr. Theunens, any specific knowledge in this respect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, I will not comment on the judgement, but in this section on Bosanski Samac, you see -- you can find another -- see other documents that actually shed light on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but at this moment we -- Mr. Bakrac is there to ask questions. And if I can answer them, I'll answer them; and if I can't answer them, I'll ask you to answer them. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, please be so kind as to tell me, do you draw the conclusion that these persons - that is to say Dragan Djordjevic, Crni; Slobodan Miljkovic, aka Lugar; and Srecko Radovanovic, aka Debeli - were connected with the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report, I have attempted to explain the connection of Dragan Djordjevic, also known as Crni, to the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, and there are a number of documents included to support that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what are the documents which would substantiate this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is, for example -- I mean, let's look at page 80 of part 3. There is a reference or quotation from P1416 that -- I mean, the story with Crni is -- is -- I will not try to explain it in detail because it's a bit complicated. He participates in the take-over, and then he is arrested at the end of August. And according to P1416, he leaves Bosanski Samac with his group for the Republika -- Republic of Serbia, sorry. But then, according to the same document, early October, they want him back. And in order to have Crni and his group back, the Presidency of the Samac municipality has to agree, or agrees, with the MUP of the Republic of Serbia to have him back. There's other documents, and that's on page -- there's other documents linking him to the training centre in Pajzos; that's P1417. And, again, I have discussed Pajzos at different sections in my report. It's the training centre in the vicinity of Ilok which was manned by members of the special-purpose unit of the Republic of Serbia at various moments in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- I'm looking at the clock. We need another break before we -- oh, no, no. I'm sorry. I am -- I'm mistaken. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'm interested in the following. I saw the document that you referred to, and I saw that you referred to it, and my learned friend Mr. Weber also gave you a document of the Serbian Radical Party foundation Assembly. Do you know that at the court in Bosanski Samac three final judgements were passed in relation to events and members who are concerned here, and did you take this into account while drafting your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing the three final judgements that were, according to you, pronounced by the court in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, there were some judgements where a plea agreement was made. Do you know anything about the judgement against Blagoje Simic, and did you take that one into account while drafting the part of your report which relates to Bosanski Samac? Instead of what was said at the moment when Serbian Radical Party was established.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I'm not familiar with these -- with these judgements. And P1416 is not a document of the Serb Radical Party; it's a document of the MUP Bijeljina, of the RS MUP Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Theunens, I agree. But I believe that in your report you made some comments, and I think that during the examination-in-chief Mr. Weber also presented to you a document - just bear with me for a moment, please. It is a document connected to Bosanski Samac which also has to do with certain sources from the Serbian Radical Party. Yes, it is P1422. The founding Assembly of Serbian Radical Party in Kragujevac --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It's a report from the foundation Assembly of the Serbian Radical Party. It's something you incorporated into your report, and you commented on the events in Bosanski Samac and these persons, but you did not take into account in your report that there is at least one final judgement in this court, relating to the events that you are discussing in your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you explain -- if you show me the judgement and the relevant parts, I can answer your question. But now I'm a bit confused by -- by your proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, Mr. Theunens, I'm just asking you. I'm interested in your methodology and the manner in which you produced your report. So I'm just asking you whether you were aware of this judgement and then disregarded it, or you did not know about this judgement at all and then that was the reason why you did not take it into account at all while you were drafting your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have answered the question, Your Honours. I'm not familiar with the judgements you are making reference to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a clear answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, let us please have a look at P1425.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Before we see it on the screen, tell me whether you made any connection between Slobodan Miljkovic, Lugar, and the state security of the Republic of Serbia in your report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not made such a connection. You asked that earlier. I made a connection between Crni, Dragan Djordjevic, and the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Since we have this document on the screen -- well, I will drop some of my questions. But since you mentioned a moment ago that they returned, Crni's and Lugar's Group left Bosanski Samac and then returned --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned, I'm sorry, I mentioned that Crni's Group returned. I'm not able -- or I haven't established that for Lugar's Group. Maybe they did, maybe they didn't; but at least the documents I reviewed allowed to draw that conclusion for Crni. And, again, I refer to P1416 for that as the basis of my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Then I misunderstood, and this will actually save us some time. Let me ask you this: Do you know the person by the name of Mitar Maksimovic, aka Manda?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. He is an individual who was proclaimed Chetnik Vojvoda by Vojislav Seselj in the -- between 1992 and 1994 for his contribution as of -- I believe, as a volunteer in the Serbian Radical Party, his contribution in combat operations. And I do remember Bosnia-Herzegovina; I'm not sure what Croatia is concerned. But I can check.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Theunens, it does include Croatia as well, but I'd like to focus on the part I'm interested in. Was this Manda a local representative of the Serb Radical Party from the municipality of Ugljevik?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I don't remember at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you recall that this volunteer group of his from Ugljevik was nicknamed Manda's Lions and that they sported red berets?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember hearing the name Manda's Lions, and I don't remember what kind of berets they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let's look at the document which may refresh your memory; if not, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, could we please have P1431.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I believe you also referred to it in your report. Perhaps you can tell us what your understanding was about who this document refers to.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found a section in my report; it's on section -- sorry, part 3, page 94, and I have referred to that document. I just stated that there was a Red Berets unit in Ugljevik at the time, but I didn't draw any conclusion as to the allegiance or subordination of that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We have this exhibit whereby we can see that the Presidency of the Municipal Assembly of Ugljevik is addressing the corps command of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The corps in question is the Eastern Bosnian Corps masking that the Red Beret units should be dislocated from Ugljevik due to an epidemic in Ugljevik as well as the prison. Is it clear from this document that the unit in question was under the command of the Eastern Bosnia Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just first like to highlight a translation error. It states 24th of April in the English version; it should be 24th of June. And then to answer your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You're correct.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because otherwise there would be confusion about the existence of the Eastern Bosnia Corps. The document doesn't allow to draw a conclusion on the relation between the corps command and this red beret unit. Officially - and I refer to the -- what I would call the Tolimir document -- but, no, that intervenes later, I'm sorry. That was P383, but that only arrives 28 of July. But, officially, all units should be subordinated to the military, i.e., to the VRS, but we know, for example, from P383, that that was problematic, and that there were areas - and again you have to look at specific documents for specific areas at specific time periods in order to be able to determine where there were problems with the subordination. And, again, to come back to this document, isolated from other documents, it doesn't allow to draw a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm striving to conclude the questions I've had planned for today, and for that purpose could we have a look at 2D230, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please have look at item 5. There is a mention of certain Radivoje Bozic, 27 years old, from Brcko. Member of the SDS paramilitary formation of red berets. And then item 6, Radojica Bozic, from Brezik, Brcko municipality, also a member of the SDS paramilitary formation of the red berets. Have you seen this document previously?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I don't remember seeing it. I see it's compiled by the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Ministry of the Interior, 4th of January, 1993, yeah. I don't -- I'm not sure whether it was included on -- in the CD you provided me. Maybe it was and -- but I haven't seen it before. I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in any case, do you agree that in Brcko there was a military -- paramilitary formation of the SDS called the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will start referring to the methodology. This is a document which is compiled by what I would call the opposing side, i.e., the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, who are in conflict at the time with the Bosnian Serbs. So that always -- that would call for caution when using the information included in that report. Now, I have information included in my report originating from page 94, 95 of part 2, P1083 and P -- sorry, P1083, which is a document compiled by -- I mean, we saw the document today by the public security centre in Bijeljina which identifies a unit of red berets in the Brcko district. Now, I don't know whether we are talking about the same units here, but that is the closest reference I have to a red beret unit in the Brcko area whereby I would attach more credibility to the information from --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. I would attach more credibility to the information provided by the MUP of Republika Srpska than to a document prepared by the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that moment in time, knowing that there isn't more between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I apologise, but I'm running out of time. And I'm trying to connect a number of things. And you always say that there should be a degree of caution that is exercised. For that purpose, I'd like to show you a Prosecution document which is a survey or a questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is on the 65 ter list, number 4533.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Have a look at the second page, please. In particular, information on wounding. So you should remember the name of Radivoje Bozic, the red berets, the paramilitary formation of the SDS, and then look at the information provided on the wounding.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We still don't have it in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But in item 1 it says date and place of joining the unit, title of the unit, and the unit commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are still awaiting the English translation. It is the Roman numeral III, item 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You see here it says date and place of enlistment and the unit -- name of the unit, and commander's name. It says: 1 May 1992, Brcko, special unit, Captain Rade Bozic. Does this tally with the document of Bosnia-Herzegovina where it says Radivoje Bozic from Brcko, the red berets?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you give me the source or the origin of this document, the one that is now in front of us?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It is a Prosecution document from the Captain Dragan batch, in terms of assistance to all those who had been wounded in the territory of Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina in combat. You used a similar document with relation to Zivojin Jovanovic [as interpreted] in your report. Does the exercise of comparing these documents confirm the veracity of the Bosnia-Herzegovina report about the existence of the unit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether you understand the methodology I have tried to explain. I mean, to answer your question in a brief manner, what these documents have in common is that they both mention Rade Bozic and they both mention the location Brcko. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. You have discussed the methodology, and I was hoping that you could draw conclusions on the basis of what I presented to you, but this answer suffices. I'll move on. Did you know that in Banja Luka there were the Serb defence forces in existence, the abbreviation was SOS, and they, too, wore green beret -- red berets?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed I remember that such units existed there. And I think you will see in my report that when I was not able to establish the subordination or the affiliation of a unit identified as a red berets unit, I didn't try to speculate to make such a link. If I linked -- or whenever I linked a red beret unit to the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, it was on the basis of conclusions I drew, again based on the context of other documents whereby I was very --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I apologise, but this is sufficient. We only have eight minutes left. There is a reason why I showed you the document with the red berets from Brcko and why I asked you about Banja Luka and the SOS formation. We should now go back to document number 1083, the report from Bijeljina. I'd like to address the reliability of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 1083, page 2 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Have a look at the last paragraph. The person drafting the note says something which even you know is incorrect. He says: "Concerning the SOS paramilitary formation, it is unknown whether they were in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina." Does this bring into question the authenticity of the information provided in the document, in this document? Mr. Theunens, you saved me some time. I do have a number of documents supporting the thesis of the existence of the SOS and the fact that they were in Banja Luka and wore red berets. I have a number of such documents.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- it's not so much a question of authenticity of the document. You could ask some questions about the overall reliability. But as I mentioned earlier -- I mean, the reliability of the source. But as I mentioned earlier, you look at the information that is included in the report and then you assess or attempt to assess its credibility on the basis of existing knowledge or, i.e., the -- on the basis of other documents as well as -- as well as the context. This last --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. These last two lines, indeed, there is sufficient information that puts that last sentence into question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I wrap things up for today, could we please have 2D318. It is also a document which came with a batch of documents disclosed to us by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'd like to touch upon the topic of the Serbian Guard. Have a look at that document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Bakrac, you referred, in P1083, I think, to the SOS unknown, you challenged the reliability, although you mentioned authenticity. Where exactly do I find reference to the SOS? You said page 2; I have difficulties in finding it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2, the last paragraph, Your Honours. I apologise, I misspoke when I said authenticity. I had reliability in mind. The last paragraph of the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, last paragraph says: "In relation to the formation called Serbian defending forces, SDF, there are no information that they were at the territory of BiH." Let's look in the original because it may well be that it's called the SOS. Let me have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, the abbreviation you referred to is in the English translation, the SDF.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see now that it's the SOS in the Cyrillic original which is mentioned there. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is the last document, Mr. Theunens, before we all retire for the night. It says: "Republika Srpska Assembly of the Serb municipality of Olovo, Department of the Ministry of Defence." The date is 14 October 1993. This is a list of members of the Serb Guard from Kikinda who were paid an allowance in German marks, signed by head of the department Dusan Zugic. Have you had occasion to refer to this document when you were provided the documents from the Prosecution that you were to use for your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to correct this. I mean, I've explained from the beginning that all the documents included in this report were selected by me on the basis of searches I and only I have conducted. So I was not given any specific documents by the Prosecution in order to prepare my report. I don't remember seeing this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. I apologise if I misunderstood. I had no ill intent in mind. In any case, can we see from this document, at least from one example, that the members of local authorities from Republika Srpska financed the volunteers of the SDS -- of the Serb Guard, who had arrived in that area from Kikinda?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just not sure whether this is the Serbian Guard of the Serbian Renewal Movement, i.e., the SPO, of Vuk Draskovic. It may well be, but I've seen various documents using the term "Serbian Guard" whereby it was not always possible to establish whether this was the Serbian Guard, as I said earlier, linked to Draskovic, the SPO, or not. So I can't establish that here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at the clock, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's time, Mr. Bakrac. Nothing else then. I just want to remind you that, Mr. Jordash, there was an issue. Look at page 8.075 and following about evidence given in private session. I think I gave an opportunity to the parties and also to Mr. Theunens to further make submissions on that. If you would like to do that, don't forget to do it and prepare for it tomorrow. Also in view of what the witness said, could you please also suggest how to resolve the matter, if you want to change anything at this moment. So, therefore, could you please -- could you, Mr. Bakrac, and could Mr. Theunens and also Mr. Weber, consider that matter overnight. You remember the issue, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll hear from you tomorrow. I'd like to instruct you and not forget it, Mr. Theunens, that you should not speak or communicate in any other way with anyone about your testimony, whether given already or still to be given. We resume tomorrow, the 3rd of November, at 9.00 in the morning, in this same courtroom, II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 3rd day of November, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.,
